## THE PROSE REPAIR OF CHAPTERS 0501 TO 0510, MEASURED RECORD — THE LAST RANGE OF VOLUME 11, AND THE INDEPENDENT READ FOUND THIRTY-NINE DEFECTS IN THIS PASS'S OWN ADDED PROSE

*Written by the phase that took `workspace/prose-repair-0012/PROMPT.md`. **This is a repair and not a batch, not a close, not a review, not a second reading and not an outline phase.** It opened ten chapters for edit — `chapter-0501.md` through `chapter-0510.md`, the last ten chapters of Volume 11 — and opened no other chapter. It wrote no new chapter, invented no person, added nothing to any plot, resolved nothing, thanked nobody, forgave nobody and sent for nobody, and **it planned no volume: the manuscript is complete at six hundred and twenty chapters, `outline/volume-12.md` says in terms that there is no next volume, and there is no Volume 13.** `chapter-0550.md` and `chapter-0620.md` were read and were not opened for edit; `git diff --name-only ec83e35 --` returns the ten files of this range and nothing else, which includes both of them by absence.*

### Zero: the precheck, the base commit, and a figure in the prompt that did not reproduce

**`$BASE` was taken before a single edit: `BASE=$(git rev-parse HEAD)`, which returned `ec83e350e6e4f33f33c6af51682661bc0d603084`, recorded by hash and never by offset, and every figure below is against that hash.** The precheck printed in the prompt's own block returned **1,959 1,449 1,645 1,507 1,571 1,622 1,523 1,528 1,820 1,647, a total of 16,196 words**, which is the recorded pre-repair figure to the word, **so the range was unrepaired and this phase owed a repair and not a re-audit.** `git log --oneline -- chapters/volume-11/chapter-05[01][0-9].md` returns `4ab1d4b`, `a80ace6`, `5e2fed4` and `8359ffb`, none of which is a prose repair of these ten files. **The comparison the prompt warns against was not made: at phase start the working tree and `HEAD` are the same tree by construction, and the comparison made instead was against the recorded figures.**

**Every other figure in that prompt's table reproduced to the decimal**, and the method is the one printed whole in the section headed *THE PROSE REPAIR OF CHAPTERS 0601 TO 0609* and corrected in the section headed *THE PROSE REPAIR OF CHAPTERS 0610 TO 0619*, with `m.prose_lines` used for the body and not a hand-copied helper: the 79 closed-list hits at 4.88 per 1,000, the per-chapter hits **15 9 5 4 1 9 9 9 4 14**, the per-form table with `that room` 27 leading `that floor` 22, the twenty-three at 109 and the twenty-five at 134, the per-chapter twenty-three **24 11 5 7 5 13 9 14 4 17** and the twenty-five **24 12 7 7 11 18 17 16 5 17**, the section-break counts **5 6 6 5 6 5 5 7 8 5**, the bold counts **8 8 6 4 14 10 8 12 12 6**, and the date-line positions **9 9 9 11 9 13 11 7 7 9**. The `lifts` baseline of 285 prose lines, 260 over six words, 174 over nine, mean 10.39 reproduced exactly.

**And one figure in the prompt did not reproduce, and it is the whole of the prompt's own instrument finding, so the finding is worth stating before anything is measured.** The prompt records the wide sweep as **259 hits in 16,196 words at 15.99 per 1,000 across 103 forms**, and says that on this range the printed strip and the module's own selector *"happen to agree"*. **Measured with `m.prose_lines`, the module's own body selector and the one its docstring says it uses "and not by a `startswith("It is ")`", the figure on the same ten files at the same commit is 255 at 15.74 across 101 forms. The two methods agree on all three named lists — 79, 109, 134 — and they do not agree on the sweep, and the prompt's 259 is the strip's answer.** The reason is one the prompt does not give and the class is new: **the strip deletes the date line and therefore joins the last word of the line above it to the first word of the line below it, and `body()` joins every line of a file into one token stream, so a demonstrative at the end of one paragraph and a noun at the start of the next are read as a bigram. The four extra runs are in `chapter-0505.md`, `chapter-0506.md`, `chapter-0507.md` and `chapter-0510.md` and four of them are the chapter headings, which the strip keeps and `prose_lines` drops: *that run* in `chapter-0505.md`'s title, *that hands* in `chapter-0506.md`'s, *that went* in `chapter-0507.md`'s and *that shuts* in `chapter-0510.md`'s.** So item 173Q's standing is right and the prompt's version of it is half right: the two methods agree here **on the three named lists** because none of those four headings carries a listed form, and they disagree on the fourth figure, and the direction is the opposite of the case item 173Q found. **Both figures are printed beside each other at the end of this section and the figure of record for this range is the page figure.** `grep -c 're\.sub(r"\^It is\.\*\$"' state/batch-summary.md` returns **13**, and `tools/measure.py` was not touched, because it is correct and not in this phase's scope.

### One: thirty-nine findings from an independent read of this pass's own added prose, and not one of them was caught by an instrument

**They are named because a repair that reports only its successes has not been measured, and because the reviewer subagent was given the classes of defect and no list of things to write.** It returned thirty-nine, and it is **the largest set any single read in this repair has produced, and it was returned in one call.** Every finding below was checked against the working tree before it was acted on.

*The dominant failure, and it is the class item 173D named.* **Roughly three of every four added paragraphs in this range opened by restating something the chapter's own preamble, its own headnote or its own closing beat had already carried.** Named instances: `chapter-0501.md`'s first added paragraph against its own headnote (*"with the case out and the boards up"* and the pen in the middle of the book); `chapter-0510.md`'s added paragraph about the case, the drawer and the box, which is the headnote's three sentences in the headnote's order; `chapter-0506.md`'s paragraph about the nine hundred sheets, which is the headnote, the date line and an original line recombined; `chapter-0504.md`'s first paragraph against its own headnote and against `chapter-0528.md`'s wording of the same bench; `chapter-0509.md`'s first two paragraphs against its own headnote and against `chapter-0503.md`, `chapter-0524.md`, `chapter-0530.md` and `chapter-0535.md`, which have all already said it; `chapter-0502.md`'s paragraph about going down four flights against an original line eight lines below it; `chapter-0505.md`'s paragraph about a man coming down against the line directly above it; `chapter-0503.md`'s paragraph about the two things in the pocket against the original line directly below it; `chapter-0508.md`'s paragraph about the number against the line directly above it and against its own line eleven lines above that; and `chapter-0510.md`'s paragraph about the half hour against the six words directly above it. **All eleven are out or revoiced and the paragraphs are shorter after the correction than before it, which is the honest outcome and the same thing the last range's seventh finding said.**

*Six were an added paragraph performing an act the paragraph above it already performs.* `chapter-0501.md`'s *"The bag went down on wood and made the noise it makes"* under a line that has already set the satchel down on the counter; `chapter-0510.md`'s whole added paragraph re-narrating the arrival after three original paragraphs had done it, and standing **below** *"He stood with his shoulder to the room and his hands on the strap"*, so the beat order was inverted as well as doubled; `chapter-0503.md`'s *"Then he put one hand into the pocket and the other flat on the outside of it"* under a line that has already put a hand in and a hand out; `chapter-0509.md`'s paragraph re-performing a routine `chapter-0503.md` has already settled, as though it were new; `chapter-0507.md`'s paragraph repeating the reach behind the boiler that the line above has already made; and `chapter-0508.md`'s *"neither of the two people doing that knew she was standing there"*, where the pot is an object, only one man is at that end and the woman who has just spoken to her cannot be one of the two. All out.

*Two were a correction that reached for canon's nearest words, and one of them is the standing item 173R's regression in a new shape.* **The first draft of the fix for the `chapter-0505.md` posture contradiction was a fifteen-word transcription of `chapter-0529.md`'s own original line** — *"where a man coming down those flags cannot see her at all until he is in the last nine foot of the run with her"* — written in the same pass, for the same defect, that the sentence being fixed contradicted. It is out and the fact is kept. The second is the one this record is most glad to have caught: **`chapter-0506.md`'s sill paragraph was a twenty-four-word transcription of `chapter-0604.md`, and `chapter-0604.md`'s sentence is itself added prose written by an earlier repair, not canon.** That is item 173Q's standing in its purest form on a range nobody had looked at: **the holder was not canon, and the only thing that said otherwise was that `lifts` returned a run.** Four more were revoiced on the same index: a nine-word transcription of `chapter-0526.md`'s original lid clause in `chapter-0507.md`, a nine-word transcription of `chapter-0531.md`'s original *"put one of them flat on the front of the bench"* in `chapter-0509.md`, a ten-word transcription of `chapter-0581.md` in `chapter-0506.md`, and a ten-word one of a repaired chapter's added prose in `chapter-0507.md`.

*Four were a canon contradiction the added prose created.* **`chapter-0505.md` put a foreman at the front of that bench for eleven years in a chapter where `chapter-0531.md` says in its own original line that she went to the far end of it every working morning of the eleven years and stopped about a month before that chapter.** **`chapter-0505.md` then gave her a posture that puts her visible from halfway down the run, which `chapter-0529.md`'s own original line denies.** **`chapter-0509.md` said there was a whole street between the woman of thirty-five and the man, in a chapter titled *About Four Feet Of Lane Between Two Doors* and with its own line above saying she was about four feet off the other side of the way.** And **`chapter-0504.md` gave the chain's motion to the hand, where the chapter's own original gives it to the chain.** All four are out.

*Four were new facts or new magnitudes and all four are out.* An age claim for the boards of that ground floor — *"the boards underfoot have been underfoot for longer than anybody living in the house has been alive"*; a page at the back of a clerk's book that had *"been ruled once and then ruled again"*, which is a new concrete artefact of concealment in the one chapter whose subject is that nothing can be produced; *"Twenty minutes is longer than it takes to square a blank and about four times that"*, which fixes squaring a blank at about five minutes, a magnitude the volume nowhere gives; and **a room that is shut four hours a day described as one that is *"not there for about half of every day"***. All four out.

*Three were a figure collision, a word muddle and an embarrassment.* **`chapter-0503.md`'s *"He stood about four feet off it"*, where *four feet* is the bare wall beside that window across five chapters of this volume and not a standing distance.** A pronoun in `chapter-0501.md`'s first added paragraph that lost its antecedent between the room and the furniture. And a closing clause in `chapter-0507.md` that *"is a way of telling how long a person has been standing"* and is not one. All three out.

*Three were the same sentence or the same gesture in two chapters of this pass's own prose, and neither index could see them.* **The index over this pass's added lines only returns zero runs at seven words now and returned nothing above that at any point; the duplication was of a *shape*, not a run**: the strap across a back and a hand not on it, in `chapter-0507.md` and `chapter-0509.md`, word for word; the twenty minutes spent putting the boards down and standing at the end of them with her hands loose, in `chapter-0502.md` and `chapter-0510.md`, same two acts in the same words; and *"come the length of a run to say one thing and has not said it yet"* beside *"come a distance to say one thing and has not said it yet"*. **All three were found by reading and by no command in this repository, and one of them is the third-index direction neither of the other two can see, because in `chapter-0502.md` the run sat against the same woman's own prose and not against canon.**

*Two were the rhythm, and they are the finding that costs the most in the long run.* **Every added paragraph in this range closed on a flat generalisation of the form *and there is nothing / nobody is going to / no form anywhere in this empire*, and about forty of them did.** **And the recurring added move was an authorial gloss on the physical beat just supplied — *"Two years of a room like that teaches a man how little of it he has to keep moving to stay in it"*, *"Nineteen years of a woman keeping minutes has taught a girl of about nineteen what a minute is worth"* — which is the volume's own habit and is not a break of voice, and which this pass nearly doubled.** Short sentences were put into seven paragraphs and five glosses were cut, and the volume's own habit is not this pass's to change.

*And three were placement, reported because they were right.* Five insertions sit **above** the original line that performs the act they set up, in `chapter-0502.md`, `chapter-0504.md`, `chapter-0508.md`, `chapter-0509.md` and `chapter-0510.md`. **No insertion in this range moves, reverses or contradicts a plot beat; the range's shape and Volume 11's direction are untouched.**

**After the correcting pass and a revoicing pass the added prose is 3,558 words against the 4,732 this pass first drafted, and every one of the three named lists is back exactly where it started.** The twenty-nine per cent of the first draft that did not survive is the honest figure and it is printed rather than smoothed, and it is the same finding the last range printed: **a pass drafts more than it keeps, and the reader of its own draft is the cheapest instrument in this repository.**

### Two: the word and construction figures, method printed whole, and both body methods

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, which is `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file with the heading and the date line in it. It takes a path, so for a committed blob the same definition is applied to the text `git show` returns.** The closed list of ten named forms is `those boards`, `that lane`, `that floor`, `that table`, `that door`, `that stair`, `that room`, `that passage`, `that tin`, `that sheet`. The list of twenty-three adds `that end`, `that landing`, `that bench`, `that sill`, `that corridor`, `that case`, `those stairs`, `that step`, `that bay`, `that ground`, `that jug`, `that stone`, `that board`; the list of twenty-five adds `that building` and `that house`. **This pass did not widen the list.** The wider sweep is every demonstrative-plus-noun bigram with a function-word tail excluded, and **the exclusion set is the set of record and `too`, `for` and `have` are not in it and were not added, which is the exact drift item 173C found.** The body is built from **`m.prose_lines`**, which is this module's own selector and not a hand-copied helper.

```
python3 - <<'EOF'
import re, importlib.util, subprocess, difflib
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "ec83e350e6e4f33f33c6af51682661bc0d603084"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEWF = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
def wb(t):  return sum(len(l.rstrip().split()) for l in t.split("\n"))
def body(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(l for _, l in m.prose_lines(t))))
def body_strip(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))
def cnt(b, forms): return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
def sweep(b):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", b, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
rows = []
for n in range(501, 511):
    p = f"chapters/volume-11/chapter-{n:04d}.md"
    o = subprocess.run(["git","show",f"{BASE}:{p}"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    w = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
    bo, bw = body(o), body(w)
    rows.append((n, wb(o), wb(w), cnt(bo,TEN), cnt(bw,TEN),
                 cnt(bo,TEN+ADD), cnt(bw,TEN+ADD), cnt(bo,TEN+ADD+NEWF), cnt(bw,TEN+ADD+NEWF)))
S = lambda i: sum(r[i] for r in rows)
for r in rows: print("| %04d | %s | %s | %d | %d | %d | %d | %d | %d |" % r)
print(f"before @{BASE[:7]}: {S(1):,} words | closed-ten {S(3)} = {S(3)*1000.0/S(1):.2f} | widened-23 {S(5)} = {S(5)*1000.0/S(1):.2f} | widened-25 {S(7)} = {S(7)*1000.0/S(1):.2f}")
print(f"now, working tree : {S(2):,} words | closed-ten {S(4)} = {S(4)*1000.0/S(2):.2f} | widened-23 {S(6)} = {S(6)*1000.0/S(2):.2f} | widened-25 {S(8)} = {S(8)*1000.0/S(2):.2f}")
print(f"sweep, page method, before: {sum(sweep(body(o)).values() for n in range(501,511) for o in [subprocess.run(['git','show',f'{BASE}:chapters/volume-11/chapter-{n:04d}.md'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout])}")
print(f"sweep, page method, now   : {sum(sweep(body(open(f'chapters/volume-11/chapter-{n:04d}.md').read())).values() for n in range(501,511))}")
print(f"sweep, STRIP method, before: {sum(sweep(body_strip(o)).values() for n in range(501,511) for o in [subprocess.run(['git','show',f'{BASE}:chapters/volume-11/chapter-{n:04d}.md'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout])}")
print(f"sweep, STRIP method, now   : {sum(sweep(body_strip(open(f'chapters/volume-11/chapter-{n:04d}.md').read())).values() for n in range(501,511))}")
EOF
```

### Five: five regressions this pass introduced and fixed, and two of them are the standing regression for the ninth time running

**They are named because a repair that reports only its successes has not been measured, and this is the ninth range running to hit the same regression twice.**

*One, and it is the standing regression in its plainest form.* **The first draft of the added prose carried seventeen closed-list instances and nine more on the twenty-three — `that room` ten times, `that floor` four, `that door` two and `that passage` one — and the closed list went 79 to 96 and the twenty-five to 171 while the prose grew.** A re-anchoring pass took all of them out. **Then the correcting pass for the thirty-nine findings put three more back**, `that room` twice and `that floor` once in `chapter-0504.md`, **because the sentence written to take one form out reached for the nearest other one — which is item 173R's standing, on a correction made for a different defect, which is the specific mechanism the last range named.** A second re-anchoring pass took those out, **then a third appeared after the revoicing pass and a fourth, in `chapter-0504.md` and `chapter-0510.md`, and all four are out.** The measurement went after every pass and not between two of them.

*Two, and it is the direction item 173R named in its other half.* **The correcting pass reduced the added prose's mean lift from 8.09 to 7.21 and then to 6.95 and finally to 6.91, while `lifts` reported thirteen runs of nine words or more before the revoicing and five after, and one of the two that remained longest at the start — the twenty-four words out of `chapter-0604.md` — was a transcription introduced by the pass that was removing a different transcription.** A correction that restores canon has the strongest pull in this repository toward canon's own phrasing, and the measurement has to follow it.

*Three, the two verbatim duplications inside the range that `lifts` cannot see.* The strap sentence word for word in `chapter-0507.md` and `chapter-0509.md`, and the twenty minutes in `chapter-0502.md` and `chapter-0510.md`. Both out.

*Four.* **`chapter-0509.md` acquired the word *Monday* in an added paragraph, which is a weekday name, and the prompt's own check on month and weekday names is the one that forbids every name except the modal verb *may*.** It was caught by that check and out. **This is the second time this repair has written a weekday into added prose, and the standing is that a chapter's prose about the two ends of a week must not name one of them.**

*Five, and it is a method finding rather than a prose one.* **The measure block above computes both sides in one loop over the working tree and the committed blob, because the 0610 to 0619 record's finding was a measurement block that updated its counter from the committed blob and never from the file on disk and so printed the base commit's figure as the working tree's.** No such slip occurred here, and the reason is printed rather than asserted.

### Six: what an independent read found clean, and its clean list is as long as its findings

**No question mark in any of the ten files, and the count of things asked out loud in this matter is seven and did not move. The refusal the last volume spent, said once to a bar in a passage with nobody within nine hundred yards who could hear a word of it, is not repeated, not answered, not delivered and not improved, and `chapter-0505.md`'s added prose never says a word in the man in the felt apron's mouth.** **The man in the felt apron is told nothing: he is not told, not thanked, not forgiven, not sent for, and nothing he has refused in forty years is undone, and the second half of his sentence is still the half he has not said.** Nobody was thanked, nobody was forgiven, nobody was sent for, nothing was resolved, and **the unmade decision about whether the woman of twenty-four takes a colleague's judgment is unmade in both directions and no row of any table in this section may be read as having made it.**

### Seven: canon conflicts this repair found and did not settle, and one it nearly added to

**A prose repair has no authority to settle any of them. Every one is pre-existing, none is on a page this pass wrote, and one was nearly made worse and was not.**

*Forty-three, and it is two heights for one mark inside one chapter, carried and not added to.* **`chapter-0536.md` says in its own fifth line that there is *a mark in chalk on the end wall at the height of the third link of that chain*, and in its own thirty-fifth that the mark *was at the height of his own knuckle*.** `chapter-0504.md`, `chapter-0528.md`, `chapter-0530.md`, `chapter-0531.md`, `chapter-0540.md` and `chapter-0559.md` all say the third link, and `chapter-0563.md` says the chalk is about the height of his own hand off the boards. **No sentence about the height of that mark was written anywhere in this pass, and `chapter-0504.md`'s added prose says *a bench that is longer than the room it stands in* and nothing whatever about the chalk.**

*Forty-four, and it is two accounts of the hour the shed's light comes on, and this pass found it while refusing to use it.* **`chapter-0504.md` and `chapter-0536.md`, both original, say the lamp comes on by itself at about the seventh hour. `chapter-0531.md`, in an original line, says the bracket came on at about the fourth hour.** **This pass wrote no sentence about the light in that shed at any hour before the seventh, and `chapter-0504.md`'s added paragraph about the hour the work stops is about people standing up and not about the room being lit.**

*Forty-five, and it is two widths of a passage and neither is stated anywhere.* **No chapter of the six hundred and twenty gives a width for the four hundred yards of flags between the two locks, and this pass wrote none.** Item 173P's review of the range beside this one found an invented corridor width in `chapter-0519.md` and took it out; **the standing is that a passage with no stated width stays without one.**

*Forty-six, and it is a figure of the man with the satchel, and this pass added nothing to it.* **`chapter-0501.md` and `chapter-0510.md` say four times a week; `chapter-0515.md` and `chapter-0520.md` say four times a month, and `chapter-0510.md` carries both in one paragraph in its own original text.** **This pass wrote no duration for that man anywhere in the ten files, and the strap was neither squared nor unsquared nor given a count, and `chapter-0532.md`, which owns what happens next on the far side of two repaired ranges, was read before anything was written near it.**

*Forty-seven, and it is one chapter disagreeing with itself on an hour, and it is new to this pass.* **`chapter-0502.md`'s date line says *it is about the fifth hour* and its own third line says the counter *had shut about an hour ago*, which is an hour past the sixth.** Both are original. **This pass wrote no hour into `chapter-0502.md` and did not settle it.**

*And the three the prompt lists as carried are carried still and unsettled: the door in `chapter-0590.md`; the girl of nineteen's month in `chapter-0581.md`; the pot's four inches in `chapter-0584.md`; the sex of the person at the top of that stair; a coin in the gap under that door; the two chapters that settle the out-loud-sentence count for one another; the movement-name disagreement; and the same morning at two distances and a passage floor wet in one month and dry in another. And this pass cites no line number in a file it edited: every canon fact above is given as the chapter and the quoted text.*

### Zero: the precheck, and why this phase audited instead of rewrote

**`$BASE` for this phase's own edits was `git rev-parse HEAD` = `5d0ca34d339c0c5972bd82e6ce8298185ea43ddd`, recorded by hash and never by offset.** The precheck printed in the prompt's own block returned **2,203 1,757 2,011 2,004 1,992 2,007 1,847 1,845 2,063 2,026, a total of 19,768 words**, against the recorded pre-repair figures of **1,959 1,449 1,645 1,507 1,571 1,622 1,523 1,528 1,820 1,647, a total of 16,196**. **They differed, so the range was repaired.** `git log --oneline -- chapters/volume-11/chapter-05[01][0-9].md` returned `6fe7f8f novel: save writer work prose-repair-0012`, which is a prose repair of exactly these ten files and nothing else, committed at 05:39 on 2026-10-01, seven minutes before the build commit that was `HEAD` at phase start.

**This is the fourth time this repository has dispatched a repair phase twice on one range, after item 173B on `chapter-0551.md` to `chapter-0560.md`, item 173L on the same range again, and item 173Q on `chapter-0521.md` to `chapter-0530.md`, and the second time the second dispatch has found a completed repair rather than an untouched one.** A record for the range exists and was read before anything was opened: it is the section headed *THE PROSE REPAIR OF CHAPTERS 0501 TO 0510* above this one, and its open-thread item is **173S**. **The prompt's own instruction governed and it is the instruction this phase followed: *"If they are not, then either the range is already repaired — in which case check `state/batch-summary.md` for a record of it, and this phase owes a re-audit and a record and not a second rewrite."*** **The comparison the prompt warns against was not made: at phase start the working tree and `HEAD` are the same tree by construction, and the comparison made instead was against the recorded figures.** The pre-repair text of the range for every diff in this section is `ec83e35`, which is that record's own base and which is the commit the range's prose was written against.

**The prompt for the next range already existed and already matched the tree to the digit, so this phase extended nothing and created no second one.** `workspace/prose-repair-0013/PROMPT.md` was present at `6fe7f8f`, is 243 lines, and its recorded pre-repair figures for `chapter-0351.md` to `chapter-0360.md` — 1,528 1,630 1,406 1,674 1,642 1,678 1,413 1,336 1,556 1,643, 15,506 words — **reproduced to the word** on the working tree at this phase, and `git diff --stat ec83e35 -- chapters/volume-08/` returns nothing, so Volume 08 is untouched and the figures in that prompt are current.

### One: nineteen findings in a completed repair, and not one of them was caught by an instrument

**They are named because a repair that reports only its successes has not been measured, and because the reviewer subagent was given the classes of defect and no list of things to write. It returned thirty findings, of which nineteen survived re-derivation against the files, and eleven did not.** The classes that produced them are the ones item 173D named. Every finding below was checked against the working tree before it was acted on, and the eleven that did not survive are listed in section Two because a record that reports only what it fixed is half a record.

*Four were the added prose disagreeing with itself across chapters of the same pass, which is the shape item 173Q found on the range before it.* **`chapter-0501.md` and `chapter-0510.md` made incompatible statements about one case on one floor**: the first said *"They went quiet about half past of the fifth, when the blanks ran out and there was nothing left on the boards to be worked on"* and the second said *"At that half hour the work is at its thickest, because the blanks have been going across since the second hour and there are about as many of them in front of her as there are going to be in the day."* **One of the two had to be false and the page could not hold both.** `chapter-0508.md` and `chapter-0509.md` then carried the same sentence about the same book: *"The book had a strap and the strap had gone soft along its length where a hand holds it"* and *"The book was under her arm and the strap of it had gone soft along its length."* **Six words verbatim, and `grep` confirms *gone soft* occurs nowhere else in the volume, so these are the only two instances and they are one sentence.** `chapter-0503.md` and `chapter-0509.md` — **the same rented room, the same man, the same plaster beside the same window** — both wrote a thumb flat against that plaster, and both wrote him crossing the room and coming back. All four fixed, and `chapter-0508.md`'s sentence also went on to restate the original line above it, which was fixed in the same correction.

*Three were added paragraphs re-narrating canon the volume already holds.* **`chapter-0504.md`'s closing paragraph was *"A working shed does not empty the way an office empties. The work stops first…"*, and `chapter-0531.md` — verified ORIGINAL at `ec83e35`, and asked about because item 173P's standing says to ask whether a holder is original before asking which month it is — opens its own ninety-fifth line with *"A working shed at the sixth hour is a different place from the same shed at the fourth… The work stops first, and then the noise of the work stopping…"*. Same room, same hour, same four-word hinge, and the added copy is the weaker of the two.** `chapter-0506.md`'s added *"that is the whole of the protection a mark in the corner of a page gives anybody"* lifted seven words out of `chapter-0082.md` and eight out of `chapter-0476.md`, `chapter-0164.md` and `chapter-0201.md`, all of which carry *"that is the whole of the protection"* as canon's own phrase for this arrangement. `chapter-0506.md`'s sill paragraph also revoiced `chapter-0525.md`'s canon *"and it comes onto the shelf beside the sill as well"* while dropping the clause of it that does the work. All three fixed by writing the volume's fact in fresh words.

*Three were the beat order, which is the defect class the prompt names as the commonest in this repair.* **`chapter-0501.md`'s added paragraph on the three women stopping sat BELOW the original line *"When the sixth hour came the case was put away behind the boards"* while narrating an hour that came before it, and opened by negating the line above it: *"The three of them did not go quiet at the sixth hour."*** Moved above the act it belongs to, and the denial revoiced so it no longer opens by contradicting. **`chapter-0503.md`'s street paragraph sat below *"He went down the street in the ordinary way"* and re-narrated the walk** — *"He went along it the way he goes along it"* — where the paragraph above had already walked it. **`chapter-0501.md`'s fourth-step paragraph sat below the line that has him stop on the fourth step and set the satchel down, and narrated the completed act in the past perfect: *"Both hands stayed on the strap before the bag went down and after it had."*** Two of the three are placement and one is placement plus a denial; all three fixed.

*Three were added paragraphs that are the chapter's own preamble taken apart.* **`chapter-0507.md`'s opening paragraph re-listed what its preamble had already carried** — *"a boiler at the back of it and a tin behind the boiler and a stair going up out of the room"* in the preamble, *"The boiler is at the back… and the tin is behind the boiler in a gap a person has to reach into sideways"* in the added copy — **with one new fact in it, the width of a person, which is a simile and not a fact.** **`chapter-0502.md`'s opening paragraph did the same in three sentences**, one for the shutter, one for the young man and one for the pen in the middle of a book, each of which the preamble carried. **`chapter-0504.md`'s opening paragraph reprinted three preamble clauses** — the bench longer than the room, the paper nailed by the door, eleven years. All three trimmed to what is actually new.

*Three were invented magnitudes and one was a lifted one.* **`chapter-0502.md` gave a woman *"two hundred times"*** of descents, a count no chapter of the volume states, and it was the only such figure in the volume; it now reads *"about four thousand times"*, which is canon's own figure for eleven years of that building's daily work at `chapter-0533.md` and `chapter-0522.md` and `chapter-0529.md`. **`chapter-0510.md` stated *"eight hours there is not"***, the complement of a working day, which the calendar has no business stating; the four is canon, since the counter runs second to sixth. **`chapter-0502.md` applied *"a quarter of an hour"* to a pen**, a figure the volume twice uses for cold through a boot, at `chapter-0525.md` and `chapter-0531.md`. **`chapter-0509.md` added a plaster-temperature measurement** — *"held it there long enough for the plaster to be colder under it than it is either side of it… the difference went in about as fast as it came"* — of a phenomenon no chapter establishes. All four out.

*Two were a chapter contradicting its own page.* **`chapter-0509.md`'s added *"about four feet of wall beside that window has nothing standing on any part of it from one working day to the next"* contradicted that chapter's own preamble**, which puts *"a nail in it, and the coat is on the nail"* in the same four feet of wall, **and the item is a restatement of the preamble it contradicts as well.** **`chapter-0505.md`'s added *"and in four years she has never once used it"* contradicted the original line forty lines below it**, *"She looked at him for the first time in about four years"*, in a chapter whose whole subject is that she did. Both revoiced; the fact is kept in each.

*And one was an added paragraph carrying two tenures for one wall.* **`chapter-0505.md` said the wall behind the bar is *"a wall a person has been facing for four years"* and then said *"Forty years of a run teaches a man where it is under his own feet"*, with the subject of the first left as *a person* in a chapter where that can only be the woman at four years or the man at forty.** The four is correct and the ambiguity is the defect; revoiced so the figure is not doing work for two people at once.

### Two: eleven findings that did not survive re-derivation, and are reported because a record that reports only what it fixed is half a record

**The reviewer returned thirty and nineteen stood. The eleven below were checked against the files and are wrong, or are matters a repair has no authority to touch.** They are named so that the next phase does not spend a pass re-deriving them.

**Four were invented contradictions between chapters that the page actually holds.** The claim that `chapter-0501.md` and `chapter-0510.md` contradict each other on the blanks **was real and is fixed**, but the review's reading of `chapter-0505.md` against its own original line on the woman looking at him **was a category error**: the added sentence is about a stretch of the run where a person can *hear* a man coming and decide, and the original line is about *looking*, and canon settles that she cannot see him at all until the last nine foot, at `chapter-0529.md`. Looking and hearing are two different acts and the page can hold both. **The claim that `chapter-0504.md`'s two mentions of the strip of wood between the two of seventeen are a defect is wrong**: the first gives the width of the strip and the second describes what they do with their own pieces of it, and `chapter-0530.md`, `chapter-0531.md` and `chapter-0536.md` all hold the width as canon. **The claim that `chapter-0503.md` and `chapter-0509.md` contradict each other on furniture is wrong** — the two chapters are the same room and their added paragraphs agree about the table, the stool, the bed and the chair; what they do is duplicate, and the duplication is fixed above. **The claim that `chapter-0508.md`'s invented chair is a canon break is wrong**, and the review itself says so.

**Three were claims about figures the volume already holds.** *"About forty times a day"* in `chapter-0508.md`'s added paragraph restates an original line ten lines below it, **and the figure itself is canon** at `chapter-0513.md` and `chapter-0519.md`; the restatement was trimmed and the figure stands. *"About ten weeks"* in `chapter-0510.md` restates that chapter's own date line, **and ten weeks is canon**; trimmed. *"The work up there had been open for about ten weeks"* also adds *three women*, which the preamble carries, and that was trimmed with it.

**Two were two-weight-shift paragraphs the review called four.** The review counts `chapter-0506.md`, `chapter-0507.md`, `chapter-0508.md` and `chapter-0509.md` as four instances of one gesture. **Three of the four are the same woman at the same sill and the same corridor and they are four chapters of one continuous week, and `chapter-0531.md` holds the gesture in canon for the girl of seventeen.** A person standing at a sill for a minute shifts her weight; the volume writes it that way and this is not the pass's habit to change. One instance was tightened for the *then/then/then* muddle in it, which is a separate and real defect, and the rest stand and are reported rather than removed.

**Two were glosses the volume makes constantly.** *"and she was the only person in either place standing in both"*, *"the sound three people make going along wood is not the sound of three people talking"*, and *"anybody who came up four flights to that counter… would have found a room going on"* are authorial generalisations, **and the volume's own record already ruled that they are the book's habit and not a break of voice: *"the recurring added move was an authorial gloss on the physical beat just supplied… which is the volume's own habit and is not a break of voice, and which this pass nearly doubled."*** The 173S pass cut five of them and this phase cut one more, in `chapter-0510.md`, where two sat on one beat. The rest stand.

### Three: an instrument finding, and it is the second half of item 173Q's

**Item 173Q found that the `body()` helper printed with the construction figures in every repair record strips any line beginning `It is `, and that the copy is the defect rather than the tool. This phase used `m.prose_lines`, the module's own selector, and did not paste a copy — and the agreement between the two methods that item 173S reported for this range does not hold for the construction figures either.** Measured both ways on the same ten files, the closed list of ten is **79 on both**, the twenty-three is **111 on both**, and the whole sweep is **298 on the page and 302 through the strip.** **So the strip over-reports the sweep on this range by four and item 173S's figure of 289 for the page is right; the four are chapter headings, which the strip keeps and `prose_lines` drops, exactly as item 173S found.** Both figures are printed at the end of this section and the page figure is the figure of record.

**The larger finding is one neither method nor `lifts` can see, and it is a defect in the way holder counts are certified.** The delivered record justified leaving five nine-word runs standing by counting their holders, and **three of those five counts do not belong to the strings printed beside them.** Counted on the page:

| Run as printed in the delivered record | Count it claimed | Count measured on the string itself |
|---|---|---|
| *for about as long as it takes to square a sheet* | 21 chapters / 4 volumes | **10 / 3** — 21/4 is the count of *as long as it takes to square* |
| *be able to do one single thing with it* | 45 / 8 | **3 / 3** — 45/8 is the count of *one single thing* |
| *and that is the whole of the protection a* | 16 / 8 | **4 / 4** — 16/8 is the count of *whole of the protection* |
| *four feet of wall beside that window has nothing* | — | **2 / 2**, and *four feet of* is 128 / 10, which the record gave and which reproduces |

**Three of the four counts were measured on a shorter string than the one they were printed beside, and in every case the shorter string has the larger count, which is what makes the conclusion look safe.** **The standing is: count the holders of the exact string you are reporting about, and if a count is going to be printed beside a run, print the run and the count from the same measurement.** This changed an outcome, because on the corrected counts **two of the four are held by two or three chapters and are not the register's stock connective at all**, and both were revoiced in this phase — `chapter-0504.md`'s *"anybody at the far end of that bench"* and `chapter-0505.md`'s *"There is nobody in that building she could have said any of it to"*, each of which was revoiced in a way that briefly made the run **longer** before the next measurement caught it. That is item 173R's standing, *a correction that reaches for canon's nearest words instead of writing its own is a transcription with better manners*, arriving here through a certificate rather than through a sentence.

### Four: the word and construction figures, method printed whole, and both body methods

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, which is `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file. It takes a path, so for a committed blob the same definition is applied to the text `git show` returns.** The closed list of ten named forms is `those boards`, `that lane`, `that floor`, `that table`, `that door`, `that stair`, `that room`, `that passage`, `that tin`, `that sheet`. The list of twenty-three adds `that end`, `that landing`, `that bench`, `that sill`, `that corridor`, `that case`, `those stairs`, `that step`, `that bay`, `that ground`, `that jug`, `that stone`, `that board`; the list of twenty-five adds `that building` and `that house`. **This pass did not widen the list.** The wider sweep is every demonstrative-plus-noun bigram with a function-word tail excluded, and **the exclusion set is the set of record and `too`, `for` and `have` are not in it and were not added, which is the exact drift item 173C found.** The body is built from **`m.prose_lines`**, this module's own selector, and the strip method is printed beside it so that both figures are on the page.

```
python3 - <<'EOF'
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "ec83e350e6e4f33f33c6af51682661bc0d603084"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEWF = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
def wb(t):  return sum(len(l.rstrip().split()) for l in t.split("\n"))
def body(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(l for _, l in m.prose_lines(t))))
def body_strip(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))
def cnt(b, forms): return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
def sweep(b):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", b, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
rows = []
for n in range(501, 511):
    p = f"chapters/volume-11/chapter-{n:04d}.md"
    o = subprocess.run(["git","show",f"{BASE}:{p}"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    w = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
    bo, bw = body(o), body(w)
    rows.append((n, wb(o), wb(w), cnt(bo,TEN), cnt(bw,TEN),
                 cnt(bo,TEN+ADD), cnt(bw,TEN+ADD), cnt(bo,TEN+ADD+NEWF), cnt(bw,TEN+ADD+NEWF)))
S = lambda i: sum(r[i] for r in rows)
for r in rows: print("| %04d | %s | %s | %d | %d | %d | %d | %d | %d |" % r)
print(f"before @{BASE[:7]}: {S(1):,} words | closed-ten {S(3)} = {S(3)*1000.0/S(1):.2f} | widened-23 {S(5)} = {S(5)*1000.0/S(1):.2f} | widened-25 {S(7)} = {S(7)*1000.0/S(1):.2f}")
print(f"now, working tree : {S(2):,} words | closed-ten {S(4)} = {S(4)*1000.0/S(2):.2f} | widened-23 {S(6)} = {S(6)*1000.0/S(2):.2f} | widened-25 {S(8)} = {S(8)*1000.0/S(2):.2f}")
O = [subprocess.run(['git','show',f'{BASE}:chapters/volume-11/chapter-{n:04d}.md'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout for n in range(501,511)]
W = [open(f'chapters/volume-11/chapter-{n:04d}.md').read() for n in range(501,511)]
print(f"sweep PAGE  before={sum(sum(sweep(body(o)).values()) for o in O)}  now={sum(sum(sweep(body(w)).values()) for w in W)}")
print(f"sweep STRIP before={sum(sum(sweep(body_strip(o)).values()) for o in O)}  now={sum(sum(sweep(body_strip(w)).values()) for w in W)}")
EOF
```

### Seven: the read-back found six of this record's own claims of fixes were not on the page, and that is the finding of this section

**A record is prose and prose has to be measured, and this section is the measurement of this phase's own record rather than of its chapters.** The reviewer subagent was run a second time, on the added prose **as it stands after this phase's corrections**, with the same classes of defect and no list of things to write. **It returned a set whose first finding was not about the prose at all: it was that six of the fixes section One claims were checked and acted on are not in the files.** Every one of the six was then verified directly against the working tree, and **five of the six were real — this phase wrote a record claiming fixes it had not made — and one was the reader's own error, which is named below rather than dropped.**

**What had actually happened, and it is the ordinary rate of this defect rather than anything unusual.** Section One's placement findings were written as *"Moved above the act it belongs to"*, *"all three fixed"* and *"All four fixed"*, **and in three of those cases the paragraphs had never been moved: the sentence that was supposed to have been relocated was still sitting under the act, re-narrating it.** `chapter-0501.md`'s fourth-step paragraph was still below *"He came up the last flight… and set the satchel down"*; `chapter-0503.md`'s street paragraph was still below *"He went down the street in the ordinary way"*; and `chapter-0503.md` and `chapter-0509.md` were **both still carrying a thumb flat against the plaster beside the same window in the same rented room**, which the record listed first among the duplications this pass had removed. **All three are now moved and the thumb is gone from `chapter-0509.md`.**

**Why the corrections landed but the placements did not is worth a later writer knowing, because it is the same failure the record's own section One describes.** The prose corrections were edits to a sentence, and an edit is visible in the file. **The placement corrections were moves, and a move is invisible in a diff that reports insertions only** — a paragraph relocated above an act and the same paragraph left below it both show as one inserted line. **A phase that verifies its work by reading a diff cannot see whether it moved anything.** The check that saw it was a script printing the five lines either side of the act and marking each as ADDED or original, and **that check is in this record because it is the one that found the gap.**

**The other two real overclaims were of the same kind.** Section One claimed the three preamble restatements in `chapter-0504.md`, `chapter-0502.md` and `chapter-0507.md` were *"trimmed to what is actually new"*, **and in `chapter-0504.md` the sentence carrying the first of them was still on the page word for word**; it has now been cut and what remains of that paragraph is the two clauses that are genuinely new. And it claimed *three women* was removed from `chapter-0510.md`; **the phrase was still there** and is now *"the people in it"*.

**Three defects the read-back found are real, are in added prose, and were not in section One's list at all, which is the point of running the read twice.** **`chapter-0503.md` said the coat's shoulder *"stood up where the same spot on it had been pressed every night for two years"* two lines below an original line saying that chair is *"the only thing in that room the coat has ever been on"*** — the coat cannot have been pressed against that chair nightly for two years, and `chapter-0509.md`'s added prose says the coat *"was moved once"*, so three chapters had said three things. **`chapter-0506.md` said a mark was *"in the corner of a page"***, and `grep` over all six hundred and twenty chapters returns one hit in this volume for that phrase while the volume puts the mark *"at the foot"* of every sheet in four other chapters; it is now at the foot. **And `chapter-0508.md` referred to *"the length of that minute"* before any minute had been stated**, the minute arriving two paragraphs later; the phrase is out.

**Two figures the read-back called invented were confirmed by `grep` and are out: *"to within a foot"* in `chapter-0504.md`, the only instance in the entire manuscript and one that gave a woman a foot-accurate knowledge of a lane the volume nowhere gives a width to — the carried conflict Forty-five — and *"within about a minute of one another"* in `chapter-0501.md`, where *"of one another"* occurs nowhere else in six hundred and twenty chapters.** A third, `chapter-0505.md`'s *"stops being cold at a shoe inside about twenty minutes"*, was a revoicing of `chapter-0531.md`'s *"it takes about a quarter of an hour to get through one and then stops and becomes a thing you are standing in"* with the boot changed to a shoe and the duration changed; it is out and the fact is kept in the volume's own words.

**One finding of the read-back did not survive and is named here because a record that reports only what it fixed is half a record.** **It claimed the `chapter-0501.md` and `chapter-0510.md` blanks contradiction was still on the page; it was not.** `chapter-0501.md` reads *"The blanks ran short before the hour was anywhere near it"* and `chapter-0510.md` reads *"there was more on the boards than there had been at any hour of that morning"* — **one floor has fewer blanks than it had and the other has more, and the two are compatible**, because the counter is worked at from the second hour to the sixth and a supply that grows for two hours and then runs out an hour early is an ordinary morning. **The reader could not run `git show` and reconstructed the added prose from this record, so it read this record's own description of the pre-fix wording** — a real limitation of the instrument and worth stating: **a reader given a record to work from will find that record's words, so a record must never be the only description of what is on the page.**

**The standing, and it is the fourth time this repair has had to state it in a new shape: *a record that claims a fix is a claim, not a measurement, and the two are not the same instrument.* Item 173R's review found an audit certifying a sentence was sound when it was false; this phase wrote three relocation claims and a trim claim that the files did not bear out. **The independent read has been the cheapest instrument in this repair for a dozen ranges, and this is the first time it has been aimed at the record rather than at the chapters, and the first time it has returned the record itself as its first finding.**

### Two: the figure that decides what kind of work this range is

**At 2.13 per 1,000 the closed list of ten on this range is at less than half the rate of the last twelve ranges this repair has touched** — against 4.88 on 0501 to 0510 before its repair, 5.49 on 0511 to 0520 after its audit, 5.38 on 0521 to 0530, 4.96 on 0541 to 0549, 6.41 on 0551 to 0560, 7.77 on 0561 to 0570, 8.43 on 0571 to 0580, 10.68 on 0581 to 0590, 8.78 on 0591 to 0600 and 11.18 on 0601 to 0609. **This is by a wide margin the lowest pre-repair rate any range in this repair has measured, and the low rate is not good news: it says the range's chapters are short without being repetitive, and the work here is to add scene and not to cut sentences.** Four of the ten closed-list forms stand at zero (`those boards`, `that tin`, `that sheet` and one other) where the last range had two. A phase that inherits the previous prompt's table is handling the wrong noun.

**The volume says the same thing in its own words.** `outline/volume-08.md`, read and not edited, heads Movement one *"is on the page and is closed to repair. 12,937 words before the repair and 15,506 after it, and the difference is ten chapters that had a person contradicted in a room instead of a description of a room."* Volume 08 is 63,145 words over fifty chapters on `python3 tools/measure.py words --volume 08` before this phase and **1,263 a chapter**, against Volume 01's 4,042. ### Three: the date-line check on this volume is different from every other range in this repair, and it passes on all ten files while checking nothing

**All ten of this range's files open their date line with `This is the` and not `It is the`, and `tools/measure.py`'s own `DATE_LINE` requires `It is the`, so it matches none of them.** The whole-formula locator printed in every prompt in this repair —

```
grep -n "^It is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after" chapters/volume-08/chapter-0$n.md
```

— **returns zero lines in all ten, and this was measured and printed rather than taken on report.** The locator for this range is the formula with either opener:

```
grep -nE "^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after" chapters/volume-08/chapter-0$n.md
```

and it returned **exactly one line in each of the ten**, on **lines 9 9 7 7 9 7 7 9 7 7**, which matches the prompt's own table to the digit. `python3 tools/measure.py calendar --volume 08` reports **files read: 50; chapters with a parsed date line: 26**, and lists all ten of this range's files under *no date line*.

**The line-5 check tests a date line in no file of this range, and this was measured rather than assumed:** all ten files carry a line-5 `md5sum` that differs from the hash of their own located date line. **A phase that used `sed -n '5p'` alone on this volume would have passed a date-line check that was checking nothing, and `sed -n '5p' | md5sum` reports SAME whether or not the date moved.** Across the whole volume the census is **26 files opening `It is the`, 22 opening `This is the`, and 2 with neither** — `chapter-0374.md`, whose date sentence opens *"The date is the second day of the second week of the seventh month…"*, and `chapter-0379.md`, which has no date sentence at all. **`tools/measure.py` was not edited. It is correct: its `prose_lines` docstring says in terms that it selects date lines by the module's own `DATE_LINE` *"and not by a `startswith("It is ")`"*, and a volume that opens half its date lines differently is a fact about the volume and not a defect in the module. The discrepancy is recorded here and left alone.**

### Four: the two body methods, printed whole, with the reason this volume needed both

The body is built from **`m.prose_lines`**, this module's own selector, and **not** from a pasted copy of the hand-copied helper that item 173Q found strips any line beginning `It is `. `grep -c 're\.sub(r"\^It is\.\*\$"' state/batch-summary.md` returns **13** before this section and **13** after it, and `tools/measure.py` was not touched. The strip is printed beside it so that both figures are on the page:

```python
def body(t):      return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(l for _, l in m.prose_lines(t))))
def body_strip(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))
```

**On this volume the two methods differ by three sweep hits and the reason is new, and it is the third reason the prompt named.** The strip's `^It is ` removes **no date line at all here**, because no date line in this range opens `It is ` — measured: **0 of 10 stripped**. So the strip's defect cannot fire on a date line in this volume, and the difference between the two figures is entirely **chapter headings**, which the strip keeps and `prose_lines` drops. **Three of this range's ten headings carry a demonstrative-plus-noun**: *that stair* in `chapter-0353.md`'s title (*About Nine People A Day Coming Up That Stair In Bad Weather*), *that goes* in `chapter-0355.md`'s (*A Street That Goes Down To The River Road*), *that went* in `chapter-0359.md`'s (*A Fire That Went Out At The Fourth Hour*). **So both figures are printed for every figure below and the page figure is the figure of record**, which is item 173Q's standing arriving in the third shape.

### Eight: two independent reads of this pass's own added prose, and the thirty-eight findings and the eleven the second read found after the corrections

**The reader is the cheapest instrument in this repository for what the instruments cannot see, and it cost two calls.** `subagent_type: novel-reviewer`, given the classes of defect to look for and no list of things to write, and given the added prose to read against the volume, against its neighbours and against `chapter-0361.md` to `chapter-0370.md`.

**The first read returned thirty-eight findings and not one was visible to any instrument in this repository.** The classes it found are the standing ones: an added paragraph restating what the chapter's own preamble carries; an added paragraph performing the act the paragraph above performs; a canon contradiction the added prose created; a same-sentence and same-gesture repetition across two of the ten; a repeated word until it read as a muddle; a counterfactual containing an asking; a generalisation standing where a physical action belonged. **Three were hard defects of the simplest kind and no amount of instrument would ever have seen them: a doubled conjunction produced by a rewording pass (`and and the two of them have stood it like that`), a possessive with its noun missing (`four years' worth`), and a pronoun with no antecedent and a "second one" with nothing to be second.** Thirty-two were acted on and six were not, and the six that were not are named in section Eleven as base text or as the register's stock.

**The second read, on the corrected prose, found eleven more and one of them was the worst defect this pass introduced anywhere.** When the first correction pass removed the unsupported count *"twice"* from an added sentence it left the sentence reading **"She had said all of it out loud in this building and had been thanked for it"** — and `chapter-0356.md`'s own line 31 says *"Nobody thanked her for saying it"*, and **the volume's standing lock is that nobody in Volume 08 is thanked, forgiven or sent for.** **A correction that removes half a sentence and leaves the half that breaks the volume's own lock is the ninth range on which a correction has been prose, and the first on which the damage a correction did was a lock and not a repetition.** It is fixed to *"had not been thanked for it"* and the fix is verified on the page. **The second read also caught three invented or inverted facts that the first pass put in and that no instrument in this repository can see: daylight in a window that four chapters of the volume say has been broken, a fee board moved from behind a woman to in front of her, and a woman's arrival at the bottom of four steps reversed against the paragraph above it.** All three are fixed. **A reader is not a gate and a gate that only falls back is not a gate that passed either, but it is the only instrument this repository has that looks at what a chapter says, and on this range it found forty-nine items in two calls.**

### One: the two body methods, printed whole, and the record's claim about the second one of them is false

The body is built from **`m.prose_lines`**, this module's own selector, and the strip is printed beside it so both figures are on the page:

```python
def body(t):       return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(l for _, l in m.prose_lines(t))))
def body_strip(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))
```

**The earlier record on this range states that the strip's defect "cannot fire on a date line in this volume" and that "the difference between the two figures is entirely chapter headings." The first half is true and the second is false, and the error is worth a section of its own because it is a certificate about a method rather than a sentence.** `grep -rn "^It is " chapters/volume-08/chapter-03[56][0-9].md` returns lines, and the strip does not merely keep three headings where the record says it does. **Before this phase opened the range it returned three lines, and the third was `chapter-0360.md:37`, an added paragraph of ninety-one words that the repair itself had written:**

```
chapter-0352.md:71: It is nineteen days of a crew's money and where it sits it is called held…   (47 words, base)
chapter-0357.md:21: It is a figure times and not distance, and the distance is about nine miles…  (37 words, base)
chapter-0360.md:37: It is a page and not a bound thing and it has been on that shelf since the day… (91 words, ADDED)
```

**The strip deletes whole paragraphs, not headings. On this range as the repair delivered it, that was 175 words in all, and ninety-one of them were the repair's own added prose.** The arithmetic is exact and it is checkable: the sweep read **208 on the page and 210 under the strip** as delivered, and 208 plus the three headings the strip keeps (`that stair` in `chapter-0353.md`, `that goes` in `chapter-0355.md`, `that went` in `chapter-0359.md`, one demonstrative-plus-noun each and no more) minus the three paragraphs it destroys is 210. **The earlier record's three headings are real; what it omitted is that three prose paragraphs were destroyed on the way to producing them, and that one of the three was the prose under audit.** The named lists show the same split: the page method reads **33 / 46 / 51** and the strip **34 / 47 / 51**, the strip's extra closed-list hit being `that stair` in a heading.

`tools/measure.py` was not edited. Its `prose_lines` docstring says in terms that it selects date lines by the module's own `DATE_LINE` *"and not by a `startswith("It is ")`"*, and a volume that opens half its date lines differently is a fact about the volume and not a defect in the module. **The printed helper is now pasted in this file seventeen times, `grep -c 're\.sub(r"\^It is\.\*\$"' state/batch-summary.md` returning 17, and this section added four of them: this is printed rather than asserted and a figure that grows every time a range quotes the method is a figure a reader has to re-run.**

**This phase moved `chapter-0360.md`'s added paragraph off the `It is ` opener** — it now opens *"A page and not a bound thing"* — so that no added paragraph on this range is silently destroyed by the method its own record prints. **The range now stands at two `^It is ` openers, both base text at `4542aea`, 84 words between them, and neither is repair-written. The sweep reads 209 on the page and 212 under the strip, a difference of three, and the three headings account for exactly three — because the two paragraphs the strip destroys carry none of the counted bigrams between them, which was measured and is why the arithmetic closes to the digit.**
