The *added* column reads +978 +635 +1,278 +249 +389 +311 +127 +140 +945 +517 and sums to **5,569**, and **16,934 − 11,365 = 5,569**. Mean 1,136.5 to 1,693.4.** The added column is run as an addition and not only as a subtraction, because the subtraction is the one that checks: 978 + 635 = 1,613; + 1,278 = 2,891; + 249 = 3,140; + 389 = 3,529; + 311 = 3,840; + 127 = 3,967; + 140 = 4,107; + 945 = 5,052; + 517 = 5,569, which is what the subtraction gives and not a coincidence.

**This section was written wrong twice before this version, and the wrong versions are described once here rather than twice, because a reader who finds two corrections for one event reads two events.** The first version stated that the *now* column summed to 16,831 against a printed total of 16,832 and attributed the one-word difference to `chapter-0374.md` having shortened in a late revoicing. **It had not shortened, and a revoicing does not move a per-file figure at all, because it changes wording and not length: the difference was a transcription error in a hand-written addition, `chapter-0374.md` entered as 1,578 where the file held 1,579.** It was caught by running `m.words_in_file` per file and reading the ten figures back, which is item 175's standing applied one level down: a total and a column that disagree is a question, and here the answer was that somebody added it up by hand wrong and not that a chapter had changed. **A second version of this section restated that same correction with a different and also wrong figure in it — 16,831 against 16,907 — and the two paragraphs were duplicates of one another reporting one event. The review of this range flagged the pair as dead weight, and one paragraph now reports it and the second is gone.** The prose was never wrong and the table was never wrong; the arithmetic was wrong twice, both times by hand.

**Then the column moved twice more, for different and checkable reasons, and every set of figures is given so that a reader can see which came from which moment.** A late reading of `chapter-0379.md` found that one added paragraph there restated the speech three lines above it and that another restated the act of the base paragraph below it — **the two standing classes, an added paragraph restating what the paragraph above already carries and an added paragraph performing the act the paragraph below already performs** — and the two restatements were cut and seventy-five words of new material written in their place. **That moved `chapter-0379.md` from 1,884 to 1,959 and the range from 16,832 to 16,907, the added column from +870 to +945, the range's added total from 5,467 to 5,542, Volume 08 from 78,108 to 78,183 and the manuscript from 1,445,313 to 1,445,388.** **The column moved a third time when the review of this range found two added paragraphs in `chapter-0374.md` that contradicted their own base and restated it, and section Ten is that correction: `chapter-0371.md` went from 2,326 to 2,319 and `chapter-0374.md` from 1,579 to 1,613, the range from 16,907 to 16,934, the added column from +985 to +978 and from +215 to +249, the range's added total from 5,542 to 5,569, Volume 08 from 78,183 to 78,210 and the manuscript from 1,445,388 to 1,445,415.** Every figure in this record was re-derived from the files after each of the three movements and not carried forward. **The prose and the tables were never wrong at any of the three moments; the arithmetic was wrong twice and the prose grew twice, and all of it is named here rather than one part of it being quietly absorbed into another.**

## Four: the date lines, and the standing that cost this range most of its room

**Nine of the ten files carry a date sentence and one does not, and the ninth is at line 57 and the anchored formula misses it.** Measured on this tree with the **unanchored** formula `grep -nE "day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after"`, the positions are **17, 45, 7, 57, 43, 45, 43, 45, none, 37** for 0371 to 0380. With the **either-opener** formula `grep -nE "^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after"` the same nine return 17, 45, 7, **missed**, 43, 45, 43, 45, **none**, 37. **`chapter-0374.md` DOES carry a date sentence and it is at line 57, and the either-opener formula cannot find it because it opens `The date is the second day of the second week of the seventh month` — a third opener form, confirmed by hand and not taken on trust. `chapter-0379.md` has no date sentence of any form, and that is a fact about the volume which the Volume 08 close recorded and is not damage, and no date line was added to it.** Seven of the nine open `This is the` (0371, 0372) — that is two, and the prompt's table's "seven of your ten" is wrong on this range in the direction of overstatement; **the measured count of `This is the` openers in this range is two, not seven, and the measured count of files `m.DATE_LINE` fails on is ten of ten.** All ten date lines are **byte-identical to `3ca44aa` and on the line numbers they held**, checked with the located line compared against the same line at the base, and **`line 5 is a date line in no file of this range** — every line 5 is a character-identification line, `He is thirty-eight`, `She is twenty`, `She is about thirty-five`, `She is twenty-four`, `She is fifty-one and her name is Halla Wray`, `She is about fifty-five, and nineteen years of that room are`, `He is about sixty-one`, `Thirty-four, give or take`, `He is thirty-eight`, `She is about twenty-six` — **so `sed -n '5p' | md5sum` reports SAME on all ten of these files no matter what is done to them.**

**The finding this section is really about is the cost of the standing, and it is the first range in this repair on which the standing has bound rather than merely constrained.** Seven of the nine date lines on this range sit at line 37 or later, so a repair that keeps a date line on its base line number can only insert prose *below* it. **The budget that gives is: 48 free lines in `chapter-0371.md`, 44 in `chapter-0373.md`, the whole file in `chapter-0379.md` which has no date line, and then 8, 4, 6, 4, 2, 2 and 8 free lines in 0372, 0374, 0375, 0376, 0377, 0378 and 0380 — two insertion points in `chapter-0378.md`, one in `chapter-0377.md`, two in `chapter-0376.md`, three in `chapter-0374.md`.** **That is why seven of these ten chapters grew by between 127 and 635 words and three grew by between 870 and 1,278, and it is why `chapter-0378.md` is still 1,070 words and the second shortest chapter the repair has landed.** The standing was obeyed without exception and the arithmetic is the honest cost of obeying it. **Whether that trade is the right one for a volume whose defect is length is a person's decision and not a phase's, and it is carried as an open thread rather than settled here.**

**A first draft of this range inserted prose above date lines twice and both were caught and reversed, and the mechanism is the one the prompt names.** The first attempt at `chapter-0372.md` put six paragraphs above its line-45 date line and moved it to 57; the located check returned `MOVED [45]->[57]` and the six paragraphs were moved below the date line and rewritten. The first attempt at `chapter-0373.md` put a paragraph above its line-7 date line and moved it to 9; the paragraph was moved below. **Both were caught by the unanchored and either-opener formulas and by neither `sed -n '5p'` nor any chapter-level check**, which is the standing's own argument.

## Six: the three import indices, all three run, and the holder counts taken on the exact strings

**The added-against-added index at six words, RE-DERIVED AFTER THE REVIEW OF THIS RANGE, and the first version of this paragraph was wrong in three ways and all three are corrected here.** The first version reported **thirteen** six-or-more-word duplications of this pass's own prose on the first run and **nine on the last**, listed nine strings, and closed with *"All are stock and none was removed."* Re-run on the landed tree, the true figures are **six six-word duplications spanning two or more chapters of this range and one seven-word, and no eight-word run at all**, and the nine in the first version was reached by counting one pair twice — the overlapping windows `and neither of them was going` and `neither of them was going to` are one duplication, not two — and by omitting one that was in fact mine and is now out. **The thirteen on the first run cannot be re-verified, because the first draft is not on disk, and a figure that cannot be re-derived should not be published as though it can; it is left here named as a first-draft measurement and marked unverifiable rather than repeated as a result.**

**The six surviving six-word duplications, with the holder count taken on the exact string from a scan of every chapter in the manuscript, and the chapter pair that holds each inside this range:**

| string | in-range pair | holders, whole manuscript |
|---|---|---|
| `at the far end of the` | `0371` ↔ `0372` | 75 chapters across 9 volumes |
| `and neither of them was going` / `neither of them was going to` (one pair, two windows) | `0372` ↔ `0378` | 14 chapters across 7 volumes |
| `and that is the whole of` | `0372` ↔ `0380` | 241 chapters across 12 volumes |

| `and the two of them had` | `0376` ↔ `0379` | 7 chapters across 4 volumes |

**The one seven-word survivor is named here as a survivor, which the first version did not do, and that is the part of the finding that mattered.** `chapter-0372.md:51` and `chapter-0378.md:47` share **`and neither of them was going to`**, seven words verbatim. **Holder count on that exact string is 12 chapters across 7 volumes** — the first version printed the chapter count right and the volume count wrong, at five. **It stands, and it is named rather than left in a list where a reader cannot tell it from the ones that were removed**, because at 12 chapters across 7 volumes it is well above the standing's four-chapters-across-four-volumes threshold and is the register's connective and not a sentence of mine: *"neither of them was going to"* is what this manuscript does at the end of a paragraph, in every volume, and the two holders are Volume 08 chapters about a room and a lane that share nothing else.

**And two duplications that the first version either omitted or dismissed on a wrong count were mine and are now out, which is the direction the standing costs something in.** **`the two of them was empty` was held by `chapter-0371.md:23` and `chapter-0373.md:37`, six words verbatim, on 2 chapters in 1 volume with both holders mine** — the exact shape the standing calls mine to revoice, and the shape the previous range's own record acted on when it found *"and he let it sit there"*. **It was not in the first version's list at all, and the omission was the review's finding: an index result that is under-reported is under-reported in the direction that reads as clean.** `chapter-0371.md`'s side is revoiced, *"the space between the two of them was empty"* becoming *"the space between the yard and the wall stood empty"*, which also fixes an antecedent the original left pointing at a yard and a wall. **`for the length of a morning` was held by `chapter-0371.md:59` and `chapter-0380.md:39` on 3 chapters across 2 volumes, two of the three mine, and the first version called it *"below six words in its holders"* — it is six words, and at 2 volumes it is below the threshold and not stock.** `chapter-0371.md`'s side is revoiced, *"expecting to be stood at a bar for the length of a morning"* becoming *"expecting a morning spent at a bar"*. **Both are now single-holder in Volume 08 and are out of the index entirely.**

**The four strings the first version reported and that no longer survive as in-range duplications, with what happened to each, because a reader comparing the two lists needs to know whether a thing was revoiced or merely unlisted:** `and the two of them` at 117 chapters across 11 volumes and `is going to be able to` at 26 chapters across 11 are stock and were never in-range pairs on the landed tree; `at the foot of the stair` was `0374` ↔ `0379` on 6 chapters across 4 volumes and is no longer a pair because `chapter-0374.md`'s side was revoiced in the review correction, which is section Ten; `and the two of them had` was reported at **8 chapters across 3 volumes** and measures at **7 across 4**, and it stands on the corrected count, which is above the threshold where the first version's count was not — **a holder count in the wrong direction is as load-bearing as one in the right direction, because the decision it drives is a decision to leave or to remove.** **Of the strings above, four are stock at or above the four-and-four threshold and stand; two were mine and are out.**

## Seven: the canon held, and what this pass added to the world

**No floor material is named in any added paragraph in any of the ten rooms, and that is a decision and the third range running to make it.** `steel`, `brass`, `brick`, `lime`, `plaster`, `glass`, `candle`, `lantern`, `quill`, `pencil`, `match`, `snow`, `slate`, `gravel` and `flagstone` all return **zero** across these ten files. `iron` returns canon at the bar across the end of a yard in `chapter-0371.md` and `chapter-0378.md` and nowhere else, and `stone` returns twice in `chapter-0380.md`, where the base text has *"the cold of them comes up off the stone"* and *"four hundred yards of stone"* and is canon.

**The shed at the Slade end was given no window, no daylight, no door and no view.** `grep -ciE "window|daylight"` on `chapter-0375.md` returns **0** and the base returns **0** as well, over `chapter-0356.md`, `0364.md`, `0367.md`, `0375.md`, `0386.md` and `0395.md`, which is the standing measurement for that room and it holds. **The counting room's bench, the counter's stair, the lodging-house stair and the ground-floor room's floor were given no material either.**

**No figure beginning *about four hundred* was written, no age, no distance, no hour, no duration and no measurement was added.** The one figure this pass did add — *about a hundred feet of floor between the near end of the board and the stair*, in `chapter-0379.md` — was written **after** grepping, and it is the same figure canon already gives that counter in `chapter-0383.md`, `chapter-0391.md` and `chapter-0400.md`, so it is canon for that fixture and not a new number. **Nothing else numeric was added at all**, and the small physical facts this pass did add — the paint gone off a bar at the two places hands go, a rack on a hip not full, a letter slot at the level of a man's hand, a chair with a man's coat over the back of it in a hut — were each checked against the volume first and none of them appears in base text.

**Nobody was thanked, forgiven or sent for, nothing was resolved, and the count of things asked out loud is seven and did not move.** **The decision about whether the woman of twenty-four takes a colleague's judgment is unmade in both directions**: `chapter-0374.md` is in this range and its woman is Tamsin Rook, twenty-four, who has stood at that counter two years, and `chapter-0400.md` is where the volume closes on her being ready, and this pass added nothing to it — the two paragraphs it added to `chapter-0374.md` are about a cold stair and an empty landing and say nothing about the drawer or the undertaking.

**The spelling convention.** `grep -roiE "\b[a-z]{2,}iz(e|ed|es|ing|ation)\b" chapters/` over the manuscript returns `authorized` 3, `recognized` 2, `seized` 1, `authorizing` 1, `authorization` 1, `apologized` 1 — the base set, none of it mine. **Over these ten files the same grep returns zero**, and `grep -roiE "\b[a-z]{2,}is(e|ed|es|ing)\b" chapters/volume-08/chapter-03[78]*.md` returns eleven and every one is base: `exercised` 4, `noise` 3, `advises` 2, `surprise` 1, `advised` 1. `labour` appears once in `chapter-0371.md` and it is base; `labor` returns zero in the ten files. `this year`, `this volume` and `this novel` return **zero**.

## Eight: what is carried and not settled, and a repair has no authority to settle any of it

**Three base-text findings in this range were found by this pass and are carried.** **`chapter-0378.md:25` has the woman of about thirty-five next door *"came down one of her own two steps"* where `chapter-0397.md:3` and `chapter-0389.md:3` put that house one step up off the pavement** — base on all three sides. **`chapter-0378.md:27` has that same woman knowing what is inside the hall of the house four feet off her, down to how long it has lain there, against `chapter-0397.md:11`, where she has never once been inside that hall and knows its shape from her own step and from the sound the door makes** — base on both sides, and no sentence was written to reconcile them. **`chapter-0375.md:5` says the foreman's job was settled *about eleven years ago* where `chapter-0356.md` says *about nine years ago*** — carried from the previous two ranges and not added to.

**Two base-text findings of the previous range reach into this one and are carried here also.** **`chapter-0379.md:3` shares twelve words verbatim with `chapter-0361.md:67` and `chapter-0369.md:3` — *"the rain coming off the landing window and running along the flags"* — and all three are base, so it is a canon re-print and neither index can see it; this pass did not touch that line and did not extend it.** **`chapter-0373.md` and `chapter-0363.md` are the same lodging house with the same woman of about thirty-five and the same girl of twenty-two, eleven weeks in this one and nine in that one, and both are base and both are right.** **The sixteen books in the counting room in `chapter-0372.md` against *about forty* in `chapter-0352.md` and *some forty volumes* in `chapter-0366.md` is the same shape of conflict, and **this pass wrote no book count at all in any room**, which is the only safe way to leave it.

**Four findings this pass made about its own prose and fixed, and they are the standing regression for the twenty-first range running.** It invented a shawl for Nell Kest, whose shawl is the second of the four women's, in a first draft of `chapter-0372.md`, and the draft paragraph was replaced rather than repaired. It seated the young woman of about nineteen at a desk in the ground-floor room, which has a table and one chair and nothing else in the place worth the name of furniture, before re-reading `chapter-0382.md:3` and standing her up. It put the two women of `chapter-0372.md` in a room with an open door and a woman shutting it, which inverts the arrangement `chapter-0362.md` settles, and the paragraph was rewritten. **And it referred to the mark on Marek Kest's wrist before the paragraph that introduces the mark had been read, which is a defect no instrument in this repository can see and which the paragraph's own position gave away.**

## Nine: what is left is most of it, and no phase may imply otherwise

**One hundred and forty-eight chapters of six hundred and twenty have been through the prose repair, twenty-four per cent, and this phase repaired ten of them.** Volume 11 is repaired in full from 0501 to 0550 and Volume 12 in full from 0551 to 0620, and both are untouched nowhere. **Volume 08 is repaired from 0351 to 0380, thirty of its fifty, and those thirty have been through between one and four passes each while the volume's other twenty have had none.** **Volumes 09 and 10 are untouched in their entirety and Volume 08 is untouched from 0381 to 0400 — a hundred and twenty chapters, twenty-five per cent of what is left, and still the single largest block of this defect in the repository. Four hundred and seventy-two chapters are unrepaired, seventy-six per cent.** Ten chapters is a tenth of one volume against a defect that spans six volumes; **this repair at this rate is forty-seven phases across the manuscript and twelve across the three places where nothing has been touched, and that is a person's decision and not a phase's.** **One hundred and forty-eight chapters are evidence that the work can be done and not evidence that it has been done, and thirty of those hundred and forty-eight have had one pass and four have had three or more, which is itself the argument for repairing forward rather than auditing back.**

**Volume 08 is 78,210 words on `python3 tools/measure.py words --volume 08` and the manuscript is 1,445,415 in 620 files.** The figure before this phase was 72,641 and 1,439,846, and the whole of the difference is this phase's own landed repair: 72,641 + 5,569 = 78,210 and 1,439,846 + 5,569 = 1,445,415, checked rather than asserted by the word-level diff in section Five, which reports 5,569 insertions and 0 deletions, and by `python3 tools/measure.py words` on a stashed tree, which returns 72,641 for Volume 08 before this phase's edits were put back. **The first version of this line printed 78,183 and 1,445,388 against an added total of 5,542; the review correction in section Ten added twenty-seven words net and every figure here was re-derived from the files afterwards.**

**Four debts are outstanding and no pass in this repair touched them, and they are owed elsewhere and not here.**

## Ten: the review of this range, what it found, what was fixed, and the four regressions the fix itself introduced

**Written after `logs/prose-repair-0015.review.log`. A repair that reports only its successes has not been measured, and this section is the part of this record that is about what the first version of it got wrong. Six findings came back; four were acted on, two were measured again and turned out to be the same finding reached a second way, and none of them was a fixture, a plot, a date line, a canon fact or a word of base text. The planned movement of the volume was not touched and no chapter was reopened for anything but the findings below.**

**One: two added paragraphs in `chapter-0374.md`, both defective, both fixed.** The review found that the paragraph this pass added at line 63 re-narrated a descent that base line 59 already performs — *"The two of them came off the four flights together"* — and then ended *"and four flights had been climbed for that and nothing else"* when the two of them had gone **down** and not up. **Both halves are verified and both were real: `chapter-0374.md:63` sat directly below the base line that performs the act, so it was the same class this record's own section Two names as the commonest defect in the repair, and the record claimed to have driven that class to zero.** It also contradicted base twice over, since base has them descending together and *"walking down half a stair"* while the added paragraph had them *"one at a time in the narrow of it"*. The review's second finding was the same class four lines up: the added paragraph at line 59 re-narrated base line 39's *"She came back up the four flights and put her hands on the counter"*, including the arrival with her hands on the boards and being watched on the last flight.

**Both were replaced rather than corrected, and the replacements do different acts, which is the only thing that fixes this class.** The line-59 paragraph now carries the cold as a continuing condition of the room rather than a description of the ascent — it comes up in about as long as it takes to come up and there is nobody at the top of it to open a door for it — and it closes on the setup for the descent: two women at the top of four flights who can hear the stair and neither of whom puts it into words. **The line-63 paragraph is now located at the bottom of the stair, which is where base line 59 leaves them, and it carries a beat the chapter had left entirely unfilled: Marn Ottery has been at that counter eleven years and has now come down those four flights twice across the whole of it, there is nobody at the bottom of them, and she is not going to tell anybody above her that she came down and looked.** Nothing in that beat is invented — the eleven years is at base line 49, the two descents are base line 41 plus this chapter's own descent, the no door at the foot and the cold off the flags are base line 25 — and no question was asked, nothing was resolved and nobody was thanked.

**Two: the closed-list headline was wrong in this record and not in the prose, and the correction runs against the prompt.** Section One now reads **7 at both ends of the change** and not 8, with the twenty-three at 17, the twenty-five at 25 and the sweep at 108, and every rate re-derived from the files. **The eighth instance was `that lane` on `chapter-0375.md`'s line-43 date line, which all three body methods strip, and the first version put it on `chapter-0372.md`'s date line, which carries no closed-list form of any kind.** All eight instances are now located one at a time and printed with the line each holds. **The prompt's recorded figure of 7 for this range was right and this record was wrong, and the per-chapter table that printed `0375 | 1` was computed on a different method from the headline it supports, which is how a total and a column can both be internally consistent and jointly wrong.**

**Three: two stale figures in `state/current.md`, both corrected there.** It said Volume 08 *"has had ten of its fifty chapters"* when thirty of its fifty have been repaired, `0351` to `0380`, every one of them touched by a repair commit in `git log --format=%s -- chapters/volume-08/chapter-0NNN.md | grep -c prose-repair`; and *"Four hundred and eighty-two of six hundred and twenty chapters are unrepaired, seventy-eight per cent"* when the figure is **472 and seventy-six per cent**, which the same file states correctly eight lines further on. **The 482 is the pre-`0015` figure left behind by the phase before this one, and a file that says 472 and 482 in the same document is a file whose numbers cannot both be quoted.**

**Four: the added-against-added index was under-reported and two of its entries were decided wrongly, and both are corrected in section Six.** The landed figures are **six six-word duplications and one seven-word and no eight-word run**, not the thirteen-and-nine the first version published; the seven-word survivor is now named as a survivor with its holder count corrected from 12-across-5 to **12-across-7**; and two strings the first version either omitted or dismissed on a false count — **`the two of them was empty` and `for the length of a morning`**, both held by `chapter-0371.md` against another chapter of this same range and both mine — have been revoiced and are out. **And one figure the correction's own reader found is not among the review's: the `equal` and file-lines columns of section Five were one high on every one of the ten rows and ten high in the total, 602 where the files hold 592, while satisfying `insert + equal = file lines` in every row. Corrected, and re-derived from `difflib.SequenceMatcher` line spans rather than carried forward.**

**Five: the duplicated correction narrative in section Three is gone and one paragraph reports it.** Two paragraphs described one event with two different and both wrong figures in them; the review called the second dead weight and it was right, because a reader who finds two corrections for one event reads two events.

**Six: nothing was carried forward unverified in the prose, and the two things the review did not call defects were checked and stand.** The count of things asked out loud in this matter is seven and did not move; zero question marks were added, and the two base ones are byte-identical, at `chapter-0373.md:17` and `chapter-0375.md:21` — with `chapter-0373.md`'s now at line 23 against line 17 at the base, which is an insertion moving it and not an edit to it, and which is the standing about a line number in a record going stale written out in the one place it bit. All nine date lines are byte-identical to `3ca44aa` and on the line numbers they held, at 17, 45, 7, 57, 43, 45, 43, 45 and 37, and `chapter-0379.md` still has none and was not given one.

**And the four regressions this correction introduced and fixed, which is the standing that has cost this repair more than any instrument has.** **The first replacement paragraph put `that building` into the twenty-five and took it to 26, which is item 173W's standing for the twenty-third range running: a rise in the named lists is a fault in the sentence and not a property of the range.** **The second created a six-word run against `chapter-0379.md` — *"and she is not going to"* — which the added-against-added index caught at six words and which the seven-word index alone would not have returned.** **The third wrote a ten-word lift into `chapter-0016.md`, *"for about as long as it takes to read a"*, and the fourth wrote a ten-word lift into `chapter-0536.md`, *"and neither of the two of them said one word"*; both put the added prose's count over nine words at 2 against a baseline of 1, and both were revoiced until it is back at 1.** **Every one of the four was invisible to reading, because the sentence being corrected read correctly every time, and every one of the four was caught by an index run after the edit rather than at the end, which is the only reason the landed prose is the prose above and not the prose the correction first wrote.**

**The gates after the correction, all re-run on the corrected tree and not carried forward from before it.** `python3 tools/measure.py selftest` **PASS**, eleven plants. Line-level diff against `3ca44aa` over the ten files: **90 `insert`, 502 `equal`, 0 `delete`, 0 `replace`**, and 90 + 502 = 592 = the ten files' line total, on every file and in the total. Word-level diff against the same commit: **5,569 inserted, 0 deleted, 0 substituted**. Section breaks **2 3 4 4 3 4 4 4 4 3** on both sides of every row. Title lines all ten byte-identical. Trailing newline on all ten. Added prose carries **zero** sweep hits across the whole range. `-ise`/`-our` clean on every added line.

Counted and dismissed with the reason, because a scan that returns two hits and no ruling is a scan that will be run again.**

**The next ten are `chapter-0381.md` to `chapter-0390.md`, still `--volume 08`, and the prompt for them is `workspace/prose-repair-0016/PROMPT.md`, which this phase created and which is the one next phase and no more.** Its figures were re-measured on this tree before that file was written and **re-measured again after this correction, and nothing in this correction opened a file in that range, so they are identical both times**: **12,472 words at mean 1,247; the closed list of ten at 34 across ten chapters, 2.73 per 1,000; the twenty-three at 48 and the twenty-five at 56; the sweep at 176 = 14.11 across 86 forms, date line removed.** The leaders of that sweep are **`that room` 17, `that building` 7, `that bench` 7, `that shelf` 6, `that door` 5, `that counter` 5, `that drawer` 5, `that shed` 5, `that company` 4, `that sheet` 4, `those flags` 4, `that to` 4**, and then a long tail at three. **That is a fifth change of leader in five ranges and a range whose defect is the construction and not only the length. A phase arriving at it with this range's expectations will find a closed list five times higher and must not conclude the chapters are sound.** **The first version of this paragraph printed the same totals and then gave the leaders as `that room` 51, `that door` 15, `that bench` 14, `that lane` and `that sheet` 12 each, `that passage` 9, `that building` 7 and `that shelf` 6, which is an inflated and mis-ranked table that does not sum to the range and does not agree with the prompt written from the same measurement; `workspace/prose-repair-0016/PROMPT.md` carries the correct twelve leaders and they are the ones re-measured here. The prompt was right and this record's restatement of it was not, which is the same shape as finding Two above — a restatement of a correct figure that is wrong in the restating — and it is corrected here for the next reader rather than left to be copied forward a second time.**

# THE PROSE REPAIR OF CHAPTERS 0381 TO 0390, MEASURED RECORD — THE FOURTH TEN OF VOLUME 08, THE RANGE WITH THE HIGHEST CLOSED-LIST COUNT THIS REPAIR HAS MEASURED, AND THE FIRST RANGE IN THE REPAIR TO NEED A TWELVE-WORD INDEX BUILT BY HAND

## Zero: the precheck, and the range was unrepaired, and its base is a single commit

**This is a repair, not a batch, not a close, not a review, not a second reading and not an outline phase, and it planned no volume: the series is complete at six hundred and twenty chapters and `outline/series.md` says in terms that there is no next volume.** `chapter-0400.md` and `chapter-0620.md` were read and not opened. Item 170 remains open and nothing here closed it.

`HEAD` at the start of the phase was **`1bdfa1e novel: complete prose-repair-0015`** and the ten files stood at **1,388 1,358 1,217 1,127 1,407 1,241 1,121 1,089 1,273 1,251 — 12,472 words at mean 1,247.2**, which is the prompt's recorded pre-repair figure to the word. `git log --oneline -- chapters/volume-08/chapter-03[89]*.md` returned **`f8170f6 novel: save review fixes batch-0004` as the last commit to touch any of them**, and `git show f8170f6:` on each file reproduces the prompt's table to the word. **The range was unrepaired and this phase owed a repair, and the comparison was made against the recorded pre-repair figures and not against `HEAD`, which was the same tree at phase start and would have been the wrong comparison a day later.**

**The last commit to touch this range IS the range's pre-repair base, so the doubled zero-`replace` assertion this repair has required since item 173Q cannot be run as it is framed — both runs would read `f8170f6` and both would return zero `replace`, and the second is silent about every line this phase added.** Both runs were made. In the second's place a **doubled-word and doubled-clause scan over the whole of the added prose was run and returns zero across the ten files.**

## One: the construction, method printed whole, and all four lists are exactly flat

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, which is `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file with the heading and the date line in it; for a committed blob the same definition is applied to the text `git show` returns.** The three body methods are given with the difference named, because on this volume they differ and the difference is the date line.

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "f8170f6"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(t))
    return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
files = [f"chapters/volume-08/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(381,391)]
def b1(t): return "\n".join(L for _,L in m.prose_lines(t))                       # selector, unstripped
def b2(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))  # body_strip as printed
def b3(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(                           # selector THEN date line stripped
    L for L in t.split("\n") if not DATE_EITHER.match(L) and not DATE_THIRD.match(L))))
W = 16462
for name, f in (("1 m.prose_lines UNSTRIPPED", b1), ("2 body_strip as printed", b2),
                ("3 selector THEN date line stripped", b3)):
    t = " ".join(f(open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()) for p in files)
    s = sweep(t)
    print(f"{name:38s} ten {cnt(t,TEN):>2}={cnt(t,TEN)*1000.0/W:.2f} 23 {cnt(t,TEN+ADD):>2}={cnt(t,TEN+ADD)*1000.0/W:.2f} "
          f"25 {cnt(t,TEN+ADD+NEW):>2}={cnt(t,TEN+ADD+NEW)*1000.0/W:.2f} sweep {sum(s.values())}={sum(s.values())*1000.0/W:.2f} forms {len(s)}")
```

## Two: the standing regression, and this pass caused it and undid it, and the measure was run after every edit

**The first draft of this range put named-list instances into added prose and the measure showed it immediately, which is item 173W's standing and it is the standing for the twenty-fourth range running: a rise in the named lists is a fault in the sentence and not a property of the range.** Four revoicing passes were made. **Two of the regressions the fixes themselves introduced are named here because they are the class this record exists to catch, and one of them was caught only by an index run after the edit and not by reading: a revoicing in `chapter-0381.md` put `that gets` into the sweep, and `that gets` is two words of connective standing in for four of meaning, and the fix for it introduced `that standing`, and the second fix had to reach for `which`.** **`chapter-0388.md`'s revoicing introduced `that once` and the fix changed the whole clause rather than the two words, because the shorter fix put `that matter` back where it had been before.** The landed sweep on added prose is **zero**, measured on method-3 tokenisation and excluding the excused discourse tail.

**A separate defect in added prose, found by reading and not by any instrument, and fixed:** `chapter-0388.md:13` read *“…a list of everything nobody has ever said to him. and he has put the list nowhere”*, a sentence beginning with a lower-case *and*. **No instrument in this repository looks at what a chapter says, and four of them had all agreed the file was clean.**

## Six: the import indices, and the one that had to be built because `lifts` cannot answer the question this range raised

**`lifts` cannot see a sentence this repair wrote twice inside its own ten chapters, because the command excludes the range under repair from its own index.** That has been the standing since item 173O. **On this range it also could not answer the question the range itself raised, because the range's defect is that its stock connectives are shared with a hundred and fifty other chapters, and every instrument that measures a run reports the register and not the sentence.**

**A twelve-word cross-file index over the range's added prose was therefore built for this record. It is item 173P's third index with the window moved from eight to twelve.** It excludes every twelve-word run already present in the same file at `f8170f6`, holds the token stream across the whole manuscript with date lines and section breaks stripped, and reports any run held by another chapter at fewer than four chapters across fewer than four volumes.

**It returned three runs below the four-and-four threshold with a holder outside the range, and all three were this pass's own prose, and all three are twelve words verbatim.**

| Where | The twelve words lifted | Lifted from | Holder count |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chapter-0381.md:55` | *is a party and a party is the only kind of person who can be told what a thing is going to be used for* | `chapter-0274.md` | 2 chapters, 2 volumes |
| `chapter-0388.md:15` | *and it is not a complaint and he has never once said out loud in a room where anybody could do anything about it* | `chapter-0165.md` | 2 chapters, 2 volumes |
| `chapter-0389.md:51` | *and there is no form in this empire for a man to object to a person buying a copy of a record* | `chapter-0178.md` | 2 chapters, 2 volumes |

**All three were revoiced with the fact kept and the sentence changed. The landed sentences are** *“and serving is the only standing in this matter which gets anybody told what a thing is wanted for”* (0381); *“and nobody in it is complaining, and the whole of what he would like to say about it once and get nothing back is a sentence he has never put into a room”* (0388); *“and nothing anywhere in this empire will take a man putting one word back where it came from”* (0389). **The third is the one that matters as a fact: `chapter-0178.md` is where a man objects to a stranger buying a copy of a record about his own family, and this range's chapter is about a printer's heading going into a case and a word that has been filled in under it in nine houses and in none of them, so the revoicing keeps the absence and drops the purchase, which is the absence this chapter is actually about.**

**Two further runs below the threshold were found at ten and seven words and revoiced in the same pass:** `chapter-0384.md:15` on *and not one of the four has ever been asked*, held by 2 chapters across 2 volumes against `chapter-0342.md`; and `chapter-0384.md:13` on *it and that is the whole of the reason*, held by 2 chapters in 1 volume against `chapter-0167.md`.

**What stands, named, with its holder count, so that a reader can tell it from what was removed.** `there is no form in this empire for a` — **25 chapters across 9 volumes**; `there is no form in this empire for` — 79 chapters across 10 volumes; `and that is the whole of the` — 85 chapters across 12 volumes; `on the second of the two days` — 16 chapters across 3 volumes; `that is the whole of the reason` — 17 chapters across 7 volumes; `and there is no form in this empire for a person` — **5 chapters across 4 volumes, exactly at the threshold.** **All stand. None is a sentence of this pass's; they are the register, and removing the register would be removing the volume's voice.**

**The added-against-added index at six and seven words returns hundreds of runs in this range's added prose and nearly all of them are one of two things: a stock connective with a low count on a rare phrase, or a run whose only other holder is the range's own file.** **The two are separated in this record because they are different defects: a low holder count on a rare phrase is a sentence worth revoicing, and a run whose only other holder is the file itself is not a duplication at all and is an artefact of an index that excludes the range from its own corpus.**

# THE REVIEW FIX OF CHAPTERS 0381 TO 0390 — THREE DEFECTS THE RE-AUDIT CERTIFIED AND THE INSTRUMENTS COULD NOT REACH

**This phase was dispatched on the findings in `logs/prose-repair-0016.review.log` and not on a new prompt. `HEAD` at its opening was `3794844`. It opened two of the ten files, `chapter-0381.md` and `chapter-0383.md`, and changed three lines between them. It did not restart the batch, did not rewrite any paragraph, did not touch an outline, and created no next prompt: `workspace/prose-repair-0017/PROMPT.md` already exists and is the one next phase.**

## The three defects, and what each one was

**One, `chapter-0381.md` line 51, a tense break inside a single sentence.** The line read "The wall opposite **gives** back what little light there is, and it **comes** in flat along the line where one table stopped and the other began, and it **gives** out about halfway across the floor, and it **had been doing** precisely this from the spring onwards". One subject, one sentence, present three times and then unmarked past perfect, in a chapter narrated in the present. Revoised to "**has been doing**". It is the same class of defect `3006ef5` took out of `chapter-0388.md` line 13 in this same range, and that correction did not reach this line. No fact, figure, name, list instance or line number moved; the substitution is one word for one word.

**Two, `chapter-0383.md` line 53, an ungrammatical count.** The line read "...and one of them has had eleven years in front of the wall behind her and the other two, and about nine people a day in a fair week go past it". There are two women at that counter and no third. Tamsin Rook is twenty-four and has stood there two years (`chapter-0383.md` line 5); Marn Ottery is thirty-four and has been on that counter eleven years (`chapter-0353.md` line 5, `chapter-0361.md` line 21, `chapter-0365.md` line 5, `chapter-0379.md` line 21, `chapter-0391.md` line 5). The same paragraph says "neither of the two women" and the next one says "neither of the two women will be in the room". "the other two" asserted a third person into a scene that has two. Revoised to "**the other one**", which is the elision the same paragraph had already used three lines earlier in "The fourth of the four is the one that can be read at a glance and the other three are not". Word count unmoved, the substitution being one word for one word, and no fact, figure or list instance moved.

**Three, `chapter-0381.md` line 55, and this one is a canon violation and not only a reading fault.** The line read "There are about four hundred yards of it between the top of the lane and the box at the Slade end, and he has been to the foot of them more than once, and the whole of what a person can do with four hundred yards in this matter is walk them." The same paragraph closes "and he has known it for two years, and it has not once made him go", so the clause collided with its own paragraph. It also contradicted the rest of the volume in so many words. The man of `chapter-0381.md` is Rennick Adley, thirty-eight, who has kept the books of that Company since the second month of next year (line 7), and `chapter-0398.md` says of him at line 39: "he is not going to come down that lane on his own account either, **because he has not come down it once**"; at line 41: "**He did not walk the four hundred yards.**"; and at line 49: "the four hundred yards is not walked by anybody this week". The man of thirty-eight who *did* walk the whole distance is Marek Kest, named at `chapter-0382.md` line 39 and `chapter-0392.md` line 43, and the two men are not the same person and are not to be confused, both being thirty-eight by design. Revoised to "**and he has never been down them**", which is the fact the rest of the volume holds. The paragraph's argument is untouched by the change and is in fact better served by it: the yards are the easy part, he has known that for two years, and knowing it has not once made him go. Eleven words became six.

## One: the construction, method printed whole, and all four lists are exactly flat

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, which is `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file with the heading and the date line in it; for a committed blob the same definition is applied to the text `git show` returns.** The three body methods are given with the difference named, because on Volume 08 they differ and the difference is the date line.

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "a9a6b52"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(t))
    return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
files = [f"chapters/volume-08/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(391,401)]
def b1(t): return "\n".join(L for _,L in m.prose_lines(t))                       # selector, unstripped
def b2(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))  # body_strip as printed
def b3(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(                           # selector THEN date line stripped
    L for L in t.split("\n") if not DATE_EITHER.match(L) and not DATE_THIRD.match(L))))
W = 17348
for name, f in (("1 m.prose_lines UNSTRIPPED", b1), ("2 body_strip as printed", b2),
                ("3 selector THEN date line stripped", b3)):
    t = " ".join(f(open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()) for p in files)
    s = sweep(t)
    print(f"{name:38s} ten {cnt(t,TEN):>2}={cnt(t,TEN)*1000.0/W:.2f} 23 {cnt(t,TEN+ADD):>2}={cnt(t,TEN+ADD)*1000.0/W:.2f} "
          f"25 {cnt(t,TEN+ADD+NEW):>2}={cnt(t,TEN+ADD+NEW)*1000.0/W:.2f} sweep {sum(s.values())}={sum(s.values())*1000.0/W:.2f} forms {len(s)}")
```

## Two: the standing regression, and this pass caused it eleven times and undid it, and the measure was run after every edit

**The first draft of this range put named-list instances into added prose and the measure showed it immediately, which is item 173W's standing and it is the standing item 177 recorded again for the range after it: a rise in the named lists is a fault in the sentence and not a property of the range.** The first run of the measure on the first draft of `chapter-0391.md` alone reported an added-prose sweep of **eleven** — `those boards` three, `that floor`, `that hides`, `that stair` two, `that going`, `that room`, `that kind` and `that leaves` — and every one was revoiced, the sentence changed and the fact kept. **More were put in by the fixes themselves**, which is the specific failure the last range recorded: a revoicing that removes `that run of boards` puts `that run` in, a revoicing that removes `that shape` puts `that shape` in, and a revoicing that removes `that little` puts `that little` in. **Every one of the revoicings made after that was made because a measure said so and not because the sentence looked wrong, and the sequence of them is in section Five: `lifts --min 6` returned twenty runs of which eighteen sat on added lines, the eight-word pass returned eleven, the next returned five, and the landed figure at eight words and over is zero.**

**Two of the regressions are named here because they are the class this record exists to catch.**

**One, a sentence that joined two paragraphs across a stripped full stop and formed a bigram the tokeniser could see and a reader could not.** A paragraph of this pass's added prose in `chapter-0391.md` ended on the word *that*, and the base paragraph below it opens with the words *"That is the half of it I have come up here to say"*, so the token stream, which has no full stop to stop it, carried `that That` and the sweep counted a form that is not in the sentence. **The revoicing changed the last two words and not the sentence.**

**Two, an instance of the excused discourse tail that was not excused, and the instrument that found it was a second one.** `to` is not in `NONNOUN`, so `that to` is a sweep bigram, and a revoicing in `chapter-0394.md` that was fixing `that time` put `that to` in its place. **The measure that found it was the per-file form-delta scan and not the added-prose scan**, because the added-prose scan as first written returned zero on a line that did contain a bigram, and that scan was rebuilt on the same `difflib.SequenceMatcher` opcode method the rest of this record uses before it was trusted. **An index that returns a clean answer is a claim about the world and not a fact about the world, and this one was wrong in the direction of comfort and was caught only because a second instrument disagreed with it.** The landed added-prose sweep is **zero** and every one of the ninety-eight forms is flat.

**A separate class of defect in added prose, found by reading and by no instrument, is in section Six and there were eight of them, one of which was a canon violation this pass introduced in its own revoicing and then read out of its own prose.**

**The eight reading defects in this pass's own landed prose, all found by reading and by no instrument, and all of them fixed, and one of them a canon violation this pass had introduced in its own revoicing.** **One, `chapter-0391.md`, a canon violation and the worst defect this pass produced:** a revoicing made for the `lifts` index had moved Marn Ottery from the far end of the boards to the near end, and the far end is where the box is — her own base line says the twine was behind the box on the boards at the far end and the next base line puts the box under the far end of the counter. **The revoicing put her in the wrong half of a hundred-foot floor and every index in this repository passed the file with it standing.** **Two, `chapter-0391.md`, a duration the volume does not carry** — *"everybody who worked the floor had known it since about the third year of her"*, a third year that is nowhere in the canon of a woman who has been at that counter eleven years. **Three, `chapter-0398.md`, an ungrammatical clause produced by a revoicing** — *"the way a man gets used to what that has been on him all day"*. **Four, `chapter-0398.md`, an unclear referent produced by a revoicing** — *"before the first of them"*, where the referents are four figures. **Five, `chapter-0397.md`, clawed word order produced by a revoicing.** **Six, `chapter-0399.md`, a point-of-view break into the second person** — *"a person who takes your money once a week"* in a third-person narration. **Seven, `chapter-0393.md`, a sentence tangled by a revoicing** into *"the whole of what nobody in this empire can be asked about is that there is no form for handing one of them back"*. **Eight, `chapter-0396.md`, a phrase left ungrammatical by a revoicing** — *"all of the difference between the two"*. **Six of the eight were produced by this pass's own revoicings, which is the cost of the standing in section Two stated as a fact about this pass and not about the range.**

**This is a repair, not a batch, not a close, not a review, not a second reading and not an outline phase, and it planned no volume: the manuscript is complete at six hundred and twenty chapters and there is no Volume 13.** `chapter-0400.md` and `chapter-0620.md` were read and not opened, and `chapter-0400.md`'s md5 is `7f4fc0446496731df81d88d745a7cadf` on the working tree and `7f4fc0446496731df81d88d745a7cadf` at `a9a6b52`, with `git diff --stat a9a6b52 -- chapters/volume-08/chapter-0400.md` returning nothing. **`lifts` cannot, by item 173O, because the command excludes the range under repair from its own index. **The instrument this range needed is an intra-file longest-common-run scan, and it is described in full here because the next range needs it.** For every line the repair added, and for every other prose line in the same file, it takes the longest contiguous run of `tools/measure.py`'s `TOKEN` tokens the two lines share, case-folded, date lines excluded, and reports any pair at six words or over. **This phase's review re-implemented that description independently, as `difflib.SequenceMatcher` over case-folded `TOKEN` lists with every pair that includes an added line, and it returned twenty-six pairs on the range as it landed and eighteen on the corrected tree.** The record this phase wrote said twenty and fifteen, **so both of those figures were undercounts of their own method and neither is inherited; the eighteen is the figure of record and the table below rules all eighteen of it.** **Run on the range as it landed it returned twenty-six pairs, five of them the defects in section Two and twenty-one stock phrase, locative or motif echoes, and the five fixes took eight pairs out rather than five, because two of the revoiced lines were each in a second pair as well as in their own.** **No new pair appeared at or above seven words as a result of any of the five fixes.**

**The twelve-word cross-file index returns zero runs.** The standing is that an instrument returning a clean answer is a claim about the world and not a fact about the world, so **the same index at seven words was run on the same tree as a plant, and it returns seventy distinct runs held by at least one chapter outside the range, sixty-two below the four-and-four threshold and eight at or above it. The zero is the instrument working and not the instrument broken, and this is the first time in this repair that a zero has been proved rather than assumed.**

**The eight at or above the threshold stand as the register, named with their holder counts on the exact strings.** *`and neither of them was going to`* — **12 chapters across 7 volumes**; *`at the far end of the boards`* — 11 across 4; *`her name at the foot of it`* — 10 across 8; *`and there was nobody in the room`* — 10 across 4; *`for the rest of her life and`* — 5 across 4; *`neither of them was going to say`* — 5 across 4; *`with the rack on his hip and`* — 5 across 3; *`in about the time it takes to`* — 4 across 4. **One of the eight is a run the record above filed in the other bucket**: it prints *`with the rack on his hip and`* at 5 chapters across 3 volumes among "the remaining 64 … below the threshold", and **five chapters is at or above the four-chapter half of the rule, so by the standing as written it belongs with the named survivors.** It stands either way and nothing was revoiced on the strength of the filing; it is named here because a run filed in the wrong bucket is a figure that gets counted twice.

**The sixty-two below the threshold are counted and dismissed here with the reason rather than left as a list a later phase will re-run, and the reason is the same two the record above gives.** They are of two kinds and the kinds are different things: a stock connective of this volume on a rare phrase, which is the register, and a run whose only other holder is inside the range, which is an artefact of an index that excludes the range from its own corpus. **One of the sixty-two is worth naming because it is two chapters of this range using the volume's own stock connective within two chapters of one another**: *`and the whole of what she had`* at `chapter-0392.md:47` and `chapter-0394.md:41`, held by 2 chapters across 2 volumes against `chapter-0167.md` and `chapter-0564.md`. **It stands. ## Six: the canon held, and what the five fixes removed from the record's own description of the world

**No new person, no new fixture, no new figure, no new plot, no new proper noun and no new material.** The five revoicings deleted prose and added prose, and everything they added is inside facts the file's own base carries: the third hour is the chapter's date line, the coat and the light and the lane and the four feet and the two flights and the grain of the table are all in `chapter-0397.md` and `chapter-0399.md` base. **No figure, age, distance, hour or duration was added, and the one figure the interrupted pass had put into a sentence the manuscript did not already carry — *nine years and eight weeks* at `chapter-0397.md:19` — is untouched and is still the sum of two figures that file's base carries.**

**Nobody was thanked, forgiven or sent for, nothing was resolved, and the count of things asked out loud in this matter is seven and did not move.** Zero question marks were added in nine chapters and the zero at the base is untouched. **No bold marker was added and no interiority was added.** The two people in their boxes stay in them. **The four hundred and thirty miles and the nine miles and the four hundred yards of cold flags are each walked zero times in the corrected range**, and nothing this phase added walks anything. **The separation holds**: the man of about sixty-one, the woman of about twenty-six at the end of the cold passage, and the woman of twenty up the river are in no added paragraph together, and no added paragraph states or denies a distance between any two of them.

**The protagonist's floor is met at two in this movement and this phase did not change it.** Marek Kest is in person in `chapter-0399.md` and is a named absence with a cost in another woman's mouth in `chapter-0398.md`; `chapter-0392.md`'s absence is the clerk of about fifty-five and not Marek Kest, and that difference from the volume's own close is carried in the record above and is not settled here. **Marek Kest is in no added paragraph of `chapter-0399.md` as a person and in no added paragraph of any other of the nine edited files as anything but a name the file already carries.**

**One finding is new to this phase and it is about the record and not about the fiction.** The record above reports that its own reading pass found eight defects in its added prose, six of them produced by its own revoicings, and it does not report **the class this phase found, which is not a revoicing artefact at all**: five paragraphs written in one pass and duplicating the base they were written into. **A revoicing makes a sentence wrong in a small way and a first draft makes a paragraph wrong in a structural way, and the first is caught by measuring after every edit while the second is caught by reading the chapter against itself.**

## Zero: the precheck, the range was unrepaired, and the prompt's base commit was right this time

**This is a repair, not a batch, not a close, not a review, not a second reading and not an outline phase, and it planned no volume: the manuscript is complete at six hundred and twenty chapters and `outline/series.md` says in terms that there is no next volume.** `chapter-0400.md` and `chapter-0620.md` were read and not opened. `chapter-0400.md` carries the last line of Volume 08 and **its md5 is `7f4fc0446496731df81d88d745a7cadf` on the working tree and `7f4fc0446496731df81d88d745a7cadf` at `b8780ff`, and `git diff --stat b8780ff -- chapters/volume-08/chapter-0400.md` returns nothing at all.** Item 170 remains open and nothing here closed it. `chapter-0401.md` is the chapter Volume 09 opens on, and it is in this range and was opened.

**The precheck found an unrepaired range and this phase owed a repair.** `git log --oneline -- chapters/volume-09/chapter-040[1-9].md chapters/volume-09/chapter-0410.md` returns **`b8780ff novel: save review fixes batch-0001`**, with `d264a08 novel: save writer work batch-0001` before it, and **`git diff --numstat b8780ff` over the ten files returns nothing.** **The prompt's base commit was correct for this range**, which is worth recording because the two prompts before it each named `b8780ff` as the base of the range they were repairing and it was wrong for both; the base of record for every figure in this section is **`b8780ff`** and every figure below was re-measured at phase start rather than inherited, and every one of the prompt's figures reproduced exactly.

`HEAD` at the start of the phase was **`653f06c novel: complete prose-repair-0017`** and the ten files stood at **1,916 1,622 1,346 1,423 1,320 1,173 1,568 1,190 1,145 1,622 — 14,325 words at mean 1,432.5**, which is the prompt's recorded pre-repair figure to the word and is also the figure the record above prints for this range in its section Ten. **The comparison was made against that recorded figure and not against `HEAD`, which at phase start is the same tree.**

**One thing in the prompt is wrong in the direction that matters and is corrected here rather than in place, and it is the `lifts` explanation rather than any figure.** The prompt prints `lifts --volume 09 --first 401 --last 410 --base b8780ff --min 6 --show 20` and says the `ADDED` line reads zero on an unrepaired range and that this is item 173O's exclusion working. **That was checked before the range was touched and it is right: `ADDED 0 prose lines`, against a `BASELINE` of 229 prose lines, 187 over six words, 122 over nine, mean 11.44.** All four baseline figures reproduce exactly.

**The one thing the prompt does not say, and which this range's own figures settle on their own, is that a prompt can carry a correct base commit, a correct figure and a correct explanation and still be describing a range that has never been measured by a per-file form-delta scan, and that scan is the one that finds a rise the aggregate hides.** It is section Two and it is the transferable finding of this phase.

## One: the construction, method printed whole, and all four lists are exactly flat

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, which is `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file with the heading and the date line in it; for a committed blob the same definition is applied to the text `git show` returns.** The three body methods are given with the difference named.

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "b8780ff"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(t))
    return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(401,411)]
def b1(t): return "\n".join(L for _,L in m.prose_lines(t))                       # selector, unstripped
def b2(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))  # body_strip as printed
def b3(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(                           # selector THEN date line stripped
    L for L in t.split("\n") if not DATE_EITHER.match(L) and not DATE_THIRD.match(L))))
W = 14325
for name, f in (("1 m.prose_lines UNSTRIPPED", b1), ("2 body_strip as printed", b2),
                ("3 selector THEN date line stripped", b3)):
    t = " ".join(f(open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()) for p in files)
    s = sweep(t)
    print(f"{name:38s} ten {cnt(t,TEN):>2}={cnt(t,TEN)*1000.0/W:.2f} 23 {cnt(t,TEN+ADD):>2}={cnt(t,TEN+ADD)*1000.0/W:.2f} "
          f"25 {cnt(t,TEN+ADD+NEW):>2}={cnt(t,TEN+ADD+NEW)*1000.0/W:.2f} sweep {sum(s.values())}={sum(s.values())*1000.0/W:.2f} forms {len(s)}")
```

**`NONNOUN` is the set of record and it does not contain `too`, `for` or `have`, and they were not added; it is pasted from the record above and not rebuilt. `to` is not in `NONNOUN` either, and section Two shows what that does when a revoicing puts `that to`, `that to`, `that going` and `that either` into a repair's own prose.**

## Two: the standing regression, and this pass caused it thirty-one times and undid it, and the measure was run after every edit

**A range-wide construction list going flat is a claim about the aggregate and the aggregate can be flat while a chapter is not, and that is the instrument finding of this phase.** The first draft of `chapter-0401.md` put five `that`-noun instances into added prose and the range-wide measure showed it immediately: `that board` 5 to 7, `that floor` 31 to 34, `that stair` 2 to 3, `that time` 1 to 2 and `that week` 5 to 6, in one edit. Every one was revoiced. **More were put in by the fixes themselves, which is the specific failure the records above record: a revoicing that removes `that board` puts `that room` in, a revoicing that removes `that wall` puts `that in` in.**

**The scan that caught those is a per-file form-delta scan and it is new to this record, and it is here because the range-wide list was not enough.** The first draft of `chapter-0402.md` read **25 sweep instances before and 25 after, and `that either` had gone from zero to one and `that marn` had gone from one to zero.** The range-wide list on that file was therefore flat and the file was not, **because the total had not changed and two forms had swapped.** The per-file form-delta scan — every form's count in every file, before and after, and any form whose count differs — returned the swap where the aggregate returned nothing. **A construction list that is flat in total and not flat in form is the shape a repair's own prose takes, and the instrument that sees it is the one that counts forms and not sums.**

**Three instances of the class this record exists to catch, and all three are punctuation and paragraph-boundary artefacts that a reader cannot see and a tokeniser counts, and all three are named because a revoicing that satisfies one of them is still prose that has to be read afterwards.**

**One, `chapter-0402.md`, a paragraph-boundary bigram.** The base text carries `…we will do the morning like that.` at the end of one paragraph and `Marn Ottery went to the other end…` at the start of the next, and **the token stream, which has no full stop to stop it, carries `that Marn`**, which is a sweep bigram in base and in no sentence a reader will ever read. An added paragraph put between the two broke it and `that marn` fell from one to zero. **The paragraph was moved so that the adjacency stands again, and the fix for it put `that about` in, because the paragraph that replaced it ended on *about*.** That is the same shape as the `that That` finding the record above prints and it is the reason this section exists.

**Two, `chapter-0406.md`, a comma that the tokeniser drops.** Added prose read *“…what he was going to write after that, because a man with a book writes down…”*, and `m.TOKEN` is `[A-Za-z0-9]+` so the comma is not a token, **the stream carries `that because`, and `because` is not in `NONNOUN`.** A reader sees a sentence with a comma in it. The revoicing was *“…what he was going to write next, because…”*, which is a better sentence and not only a compliant one.

**Three, `chapter-0410.md` and `chapter-0409.md`, the same class twice more.** *“…a shape like that in it…”* gave `that in`, and *“…she had not arranged that either…”* gave `that either`. `that in` is excused by being in `NONNOUN` as `in`, and `that either` is not excused at all.

**The measure was run after every single edit and not once at the end, and the per-file form delta was empty before the range was committed and empty after, in both directions, in all ten files.** The added-prose sweep on this range's own ninety-eight added lines, scanned on method-3 tokenisation: **zero**. The doubled-word scan inside a single added paragraph: **one hit, `it It` at `chapter-0406.md:31`, and it is the two halves of a sentence boundary — *“who has come to it. It was not a discovery.”* — and it is named here rather than tidied away.**

**Volume 09 is 74,127 words and the manuscript is 1,458,716 in 620 files on `python3 tools/measure.py words`.** The figures before this phase were 69,362 and 1,453,951, and the whole of the difference is this phase's own landed repair: **69,362 + 4,765 = 74,127 and 1,453,951 + 4,765 = 1,458,716, checked rather than asserted by the word-level diff in section Five, which reports 4,765 words across 98 inserted lines with 0 deletions and 0 substitutions, and by `git diff -U0 b8780ff` over the ten edited files piped through `wc -w` on the added lines, which returns 4,765.** Volume 09 is **1,483 words a chapter** after this phase and was 1,387 before it.

The first movement was the reading pass of section Six, which found seven restatements and one interiority and which took the range to **19,090**. **The removed words are the price of eight findings on a range whose added prose is nearly five thousand words long, and the range is seventy-seven words shorter for having had them found, which is the same shape as item 176's correction and is the honest cost of a finding.** Every figure in this record was re-derived from the files after each movement and not carried forward.

## Four: the date lines, and this volume puts them where a repair has room, and the located check is still the standing

**All ten files carry a date sentence and all ten open `It is`, at lines 7, 9, 7, 9, 7, 7, 9, 9, 9 and 7, and all ten are byte-identical to `b8780ff` and on the line numbers they held**, checked with the located line compared against the same line at the base, line by line and not by count. **`calendar --volume 09` reports 50 files read and 50 date lines parsed with none unparsed, and this is the first volume in this repair whose printed instrument sees every file.** The instrument was not edited and the located check was not replaced by it.

**`line 5` is a date line in no file of this range and every one of the ten carries prose there — `chapter-0401.md`'s line 5 is a bolded paragraph and `chapter-0402.md`'s is the line that names Tamsin Rook — so `sed -n '5p' | md5sum` returns a hash and not a verdict and would return the same answer however the file were edited.** That is the fifth range running on which the printed line-5 check has been blind, and **the standing is unchanged: the located check is the standing and not the printed one, and a volume whose printed instrument happens to agree is not a reason to stop checking.**

**And this phase broke the standing once, which is the argument for keeping it.** The first draft inserted a paragraph after base line 3 of `chapter-0403.md`, which is **above** that file's date line at line 7, and the date line moved from 7 to 9. The located check found it immediately, the paragraph was moved below the first section break, and the date line returned to 7. **The same mistake was caught a second time in the same ten minutes on `chapter-0407.md` at base line 3 against a date line at 9, and the helper was then changed to refuse any insert above a located date line, which is the transferable half of this section.**
