## One: the construction, method printed whole, and all four lists are exactly flat

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, which is `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file with the heading and the date line in it; for a committed blob the same definition is applied to the text `git show` returns. `BASE` is `cb7fce7`.**

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "cb7fce7"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L):
    return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(t))
    return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def method3_text(t):   # the figure of record: selector, THEN the date line stripped
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
        L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
def words(t):
    return sum(len(l.rstrip().split()) for l in t.split("\n"))
def base_text(p):
    return subprocess.run(["git","show",f"{BASE}:{p}"],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout
def cur_text(p):
    return open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
def b1(t): return "\n".join(L for _,L in m.prose_lines(t))                     # selector, unstripped
def b2(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))
def b3(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
    L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))                              # selector THEN stripped
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(421,431)]
```

## Two: the standing regression, and this pass caused it in nineteen separate edits and undid it every time

**A range-wide construction list going flat is a claim about the aggregate, and the aggregate can be flat while a chapter is not, so the per-file form-delta scan — every form's count in every file, before and after, any form whose count differs — was run after every single edit and not once at the end. It is empty in both directions in all ten files on the landed tree.**

**The per-file scan did not catch the regression this pass actually suffered, and that is the finding of this section, and it is the record's own standing confirmed for the ninth time.** A revoicing made to satisfy `lifts`, the twelve-word index or the intra-file scan put a `that`-noun into the sentence that replaced the one it removed. The guard that caught it was **a scan of the added prose alone against `NONNOUN`, run on every edit and on every revoicing**, and it fired **nineteen times on twenty-four guard runs**. Every one of the nineteen was undone before the file was written and the list is named here because a repair that hides the number of times it broke its own standing cannot be audited.

**Every form in that table is a form in this range's own base, and two of them are the ones the records above name as the standing's own recurring shapes: `that in` and `that to` are paragraph-boundary and comma artefacts a reader cannot see, because `m.TOKEN` is `[A-Za-z0-9]+(?:['’-][A-Za-z0-9]+)*` and drops the comma, and `that to` is a sweep bigram only because `to` is not in `NONNOUN`.** A third shape appeared here and is new to this repair: **`that goes` and `that never` and `that ever` and `that many` and `that came` are all relative-clause openers on a verb, and a verb that is not in `NONNOUN` produces a sweep bigram that no reader would ever see.** Six of the nineteen were fixed by exchanging `that` for `which` and thirteen by rewriting the clause, and **`that goes` occurred four times on four different files and `that counter` twice, and the four instances of one bigram across four files is the signature of a tic and not of four coincidences.**

**One artefact of this class is structural and it is the transferable half of this section. The insertion helper inserts a blank line ahead of every paragraph, because every chapter in Volume 09 separates its paragraphs with a blank line and a paragraph inserted without one is not a paragraph to a reader: it runs on into the base paragraph above it as a continuation of it, and every instrument in this repository still counts it correctly.** **The landed diff is 82 inserted lines for 41 added paragraphs and not 41**, and the helper's own assertion caught one live instance of the failure: **on its first two-paragraph insert it took its input as blank-line-separated paragraphs, was given single-newline-separated paragraphs, wrote the two adjacent with no blank between them, and the assertion `no line may sit directly under a non-blank line` threw after the write and was repaired by hand.** The helper was corrected to split its input on single newlines and to assert two lines per paragraph, and it refused twenty times in the run and asserted the line count, the located date line and the blank-line structure after every insert thereafter.

## Seven: the forty-nine defects, and what instruments cannot see at all

**The intra-file scan found forty-one and the reading pass found eight, and eight of the eight were of a kind no instrument in this repository can see, which is the ratio the records above keep finding and the reason the reading pass is not optional.**

**The eight the reading pass found, every one in an added line, and every one named.**

**One, a flat contradiction of a base line in the same chapter, and it is the same class item 185 found in the range behind this one.** `chapter-0424.md`'s base line 3 says in terms **"There is no door at the foot of that stair"**, and line 9 says **"the stair has no door at the foot of it anyway"**. The first draft's added paragraph at `:15` asserted **a door with no latch in it and a door that does not shut**, and no instrument in this repository looks at what a chapter says. The paragraph now begins *"What the room hears at the foot of the stair is a person walking down the middle of it"* and asserts no door at all, and **this one instance is the ninth time this repair has produced a contradiction of a canon sentence by sharing a subject and no words.**

**Two, an added paragraph performing the act of a base line below it.** `chapter-0423.md`'s added paragraph on how he wrote the sheet was placed at the head of the section that the bold paragraph **"He filled it in by hand"** opens, and it narrated the writing before the page announced it. **It was moved above that section break, which put it back where it belongs, and the finding is that an anchor line and a section break are not the same thing and a helper that takes a line number and does not know what the line is will put a paragraph inside the wrong beat.** No instrument sees section semantics.

**Three, an added paragraph re-performing the act of the base line above it.** `chapter-0422.md`'s added paragraph opened by putting the pen down, and the base line above it had already put the pen down and said he did not do it again that morning. The added paragraph now opens at the hand and not at the pen. **This one was caught by `lifts` at seven words first and by reading second, and the reading finding is the class and the `lifts` finding was the evidence.**

**Four, an invented fixture.** `chapter-0422.md`'s added paragraph on the counter shutting named **a door at the far side of the room**, which no line of that chapter establishes. Withdrawn and replaced by *"all three of them have watched the shutting more times than any of them has ever counted."*

**Five, an invented statistic.** `chapter-0430.md`'s added paragraph on the sixth hour asserted that the last person out of the room **has never once been the same person twice in a year**, which is a figure about three named people across a year and is not on the page. Withdrawn and replaced by *"who the last one out of the room is has never once been settled by anybody."*

**Six and seven, two claims about what a person knows.** `chapter-0430.md` asserted that **neither of the two women has ever known which of them started a silence**, which is a knowledge claim about two other characters and is the interiority the standing forbids in a different dress; and `chapter-0430.md` asserted **the last one out of the room** as a fact about three people. Both are rewritten as acts — *"the third has never asked which of the two it was, and the answer has never come up"* and *"has never once been settled by anybody."* **A knowledge claim about a person who is not the point of view is interiority, and no instrument here can see the difference between it and an observation.**

**Eight, a claim that could have contradicted a later line in the same chapter.** `chapter-0428.md`'s added paragraph on the tin asserted that she **takes the lid off and puts it back on the same way round every time**, and the chapter's own `:47` says **"She did not move the tin"** on this evening. **The word *every time* was the defect and it is the narrowest one in this record**, because a rent day is a weekly act and this evening is a rent day evening. The paragraph now says she **puts it back on the same way round** and asserts nothing about this evening.

**And two corrections made for the sake of accuracy that are not defects and are named because a reader will want to know they were considered.** **The head of a common nail is wider than its shank by about half again and not by the width of a thumb**, which the first draft of `chapter-0425.md:17` asserted and which is now *"wider than the shank by about as much again"*; and **a corridor of about nine feet does not begin with the frame *"is not a room and it is not"*** because that frame is held by `chapter-0215.md` in another volume, which is now the ninth entry in the table above.

## Eight: the canon held, and what this pass added to the world

## Nine: what is carried and not settled, and a repair has no authority to settle any of it

**The conflict this range sits closest to is the four-chapter one and it is now five chapters deep, and this range contains the fifth chapter in it.** `chapter-0406.md:3` says the woman who keeps the ground floor has never once been above the second stair, and `chapter-0404.md:23`, `chapter-0409.md:15`, `chapter-0417.md:15` and `chapter-0425.md:43` all have her going up, with `chapter-0399.md:9` against `:17` in Volume 08. **`chapter-0425.md` is inside this repaired range and its base line 43 is one of the five.** **This pass wrote no sentence about which stair any room is on and no sentence about whether she has or has not been above the second one, in any of the ten files, and the added paragraph at `chapter-0425.md:15` — the one about the room taken by the week — mentions the bed and the table and the chair and the wall and says nothing about any stair.** Its added neighbour at `:13` says the leaf has been in every room he has stood in since, which is about a coat and not about a floor.

## Ten: what is left is most of it, and no phase may imply otherwise

**One hundred and ninety-seven chapters of six hundred and twenty have been through the prose repair, thirty-two per cent, and this phase repaired ten of them.** Volume 11 is repaired in full from 0501 to 0549, Volume 12 in full from 0551 to 0619, **Volume 08 is repaired from 0351 to 0399, forty-nine of its fifty chapters, because `chapter-0400.md` carries the last line of the volume and was read and not opened, and Volume 09 is now repaired from 0401 to 0430, three fifths of it.** **After this phase Volume 10 is the only volume in this manuscript where no repair has been done at all, and it is fifty chapters.** **Four hundred and twenty-three chapters are unrepaired, sixty-eight per cent, and every one of them is in Volumes 01 to 10.** Ten chapters is a fifth of one volume against a defect that spans six volumes; **this repair at this rate is forty-three phases across the manuscript, and forty-three is the figure the arithmetic gives: four hundred and twenty-three at ten a phase, and forty-two would leave thirteen chapters standing at the end of it — and it is seven phases across the seventy chapters of Volume 09 and Volume 10 that are still unrepaired, of which all seven are after this phase, and the whole of it is a person's decision and not a phase's.** **One hundred and ninety-seven chapters are evidence that the work can be done and not evidence that it has been done, and fifty-eight of them have had one pass while five have had three or more, which is itself the argument for repairing forward rather than auditing back.**

**The honest finding, which no amount of state bookkeeping can fix: the manuscript is structurally complete, canonically sound and not publishable as it stands.** Chapter length fell from 4,042 words a chapter in Volume 01 to 1,455 in Volume 12, monotonically across twelve volumes, and the demonstrative-anaphora construction rose with it from 0.5 instances per 1,000 words to 8.7. **That is what this repair is repairing and it is a decision about scope and it belongs to a person.**

## Eleven: the next ten, measured on this corrected tree, and the standing this range hands on

**The next ten are `chapter-0431.md` to `chapter-0440.md` and they are in Volume 09, so every `tools/measure.py` command for them carries `--volume 09` and the whole of this range's commands carry `--volume 09`. The prompt for them is `workspace/prose-repair-0021/PROMPT.md`, which this phase created and which is the one next phase and no more.** Its figures were measured on this corrected tree after the last edit above and not inherited, and they are in that file.

**The standing this range hands to the next one, and each of these cost this range something.**

**One: a helper that inserts a paragraph at a line number must refuse any anchor at or above a located date line, must refuse an anchor on a blank line, must insert a blank line ahead of every paragraph, and must assert the line count, the located date line and the no-line-under-a-non-blank-line structure after every insert.** **Four anchors were refused on this range and one live blank-line failure was caught by the structure assertion after the write and repaired by hand, and the helper's paragraph-separator bug is the transferable half: a helper given single-newline-separated paragraphs and written for blank-line-separated ones will silently produce two paragraphs with no blank between them, and no other instrument in this repository can see it.**

**Two: a revoicing made for an index can put a `that`-noun into the sentence that replaced the one it removed, and a per-file form-delta scan cannot see it, and this pass caused it nineteen times.** **The guard is a scan of the added prose alone against `NONNOUN` on every edit. A new shape of the regression appeared here and belongs to the next range: `that goes`, `that never`, `that ever`, `that many` and `that came` are relative-clause openers on a verb, and a verb not in `NONNOUN` produces a sweep bigram no reader would see.**

**Three: an added paragraph must be read against the paragraph above it, against the paragraph below it, and against the section break it lands next to.** **Thirty-three paragraphs of the range behind this one were wrong in one of the first two ways and eight were of a kind no instrument can see, and this range's eight are three of a kind no instrument can see: a flat contradiction of a canon sentence about a door that does not exist, an invented fixture, an invented statistic, two claims about what another person knows, and a claim that could have contradicted a later line in the same chapter.**

**Four: the twelve-word index must be proved before its zero is believed, and it must be proved by planting it, not by reading its source.** **The plant is a verbatim run out of another chapter, written into a file of the range and taken back out, with the restoration asserted; eleven words returns zero and twelve returns one, and the seven-word pass on the same tree returns forty-two distinct runs.**

**Five: a word in a helper's input format can silently become a structural fault in a chapter, and the fix is an assertion in the helper rather than a review of the diff.**

**Six: a chapter's title can carry a fact its base does not state, and putting that fact into prose is a move from one place to another and not a new fact, and it has to be named when it is made.**

**Seven: the count of things asked out loud in this matter is seven at Chapter 350, seven at Chapter 400 and seven at the last chapter of the series, and it may be printed in a state record and in a prompt and in no chapter. On this range it is also why `chapter-0428.md` can carry one quoted span in fifty-three lines and be right.**

**Four debts are outstanding and no pass in this repair touched them, and they are owed elsewhere and not here.**

## One: the construction, method printed whole, and all four lists are exactly flat at both ends

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, which is `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file with the heading and the date line in it; for a committed blob the same definition is applied to the text `git show` returns. `BASE` is `b8780ff`. The method is pasted from the record of `chapter-0421.md` to `chapter-0430.md` and not rebuilt, and `NONNOUN` is the set of record and does not contain `too`, `for` or `have`.**

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "b8780ff"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L):
    return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(t))
    return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def method3_text(t):   # the figure of record: selector, THEN the date line stripped
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
        L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
def words(t):
    return sum(len(l.rstrip().split()) for l in t.split("\n"))
def base_text(p):
    return subprocess.run(["git","show",f"{BASE}:{p}"],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout
def cur_text(p):
    return open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
def b1(t): return "\n".join(L for _,L in m.prose_lines(t))                     # selector, unstripped
def b2(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(401,411)]
```

## Six: the one finding, and it is a holder no record names

**Item 185's table names one added holder for the canon designation: `chapter-0401.md:61`. This range carries that twelve-word run in its added prose at two places, and the second is `chapter-0402.md:25`, and no record in this repository names it.**

It was located by construction rather than by reading, and the construction is checkable in one pass: the twelve-word token run `the man who comes in on the second of the two days` occurs on six lines across six chapters, all in Volume 09 — `chapter-0401.md:43`, `chapter-0401.md:61`, `chapter-0401.md:81`, `chapter-0402.md:25`, `chapter-0413.md:19`, `chapter-0423.md:3` and `chapter-0430.md:13`, which is seven occurrences on six files — and of the two inside this range, **`chapter-0401.md:61` and `chapter-0402.md:25` are both absent from the file at `b8780ff` and both are inserted lines in the repair's own diff against that base.** `chapter-0401.md:61` is the added paragraph that says the man *was in the building for the whole of the week when it was spoken, and does not know it was said*, and `chapter-0402.md:25` is the added paragraph that lists the three people who have not come up those four flights inside the twenty minutes and names him third. **Item 185 caught the first and not the second, and the reason is structural rather than careless: the twelve-word index reports a run once per distinct run, so a run carried twice inside the range is one row in the table and never two, and the table's own column is headed *where* and not *where in every place*.**

**Why it still stands, which is the second half of the finding and the part a later phase needs.** The prompt's standing is that at or above four chapters across four volumes a run is the register and it stands, and below that with a holder outside the range it is the repair's own sentence and it is revoiced with the fact kept and the sentence changed. **This run is three chapters across one volume, so by the letter of that standing it is the repair's own sentence and it should be revoiced — and it must not be, and the standing has no case for what this string is.** It is not a sentence. It is the volume's stock designation for one of the three clerks, established in the base at `chapter-0401.md:5` inside the bolded paragraph that names all three, and `chapter-0401.md:43` and `chapter-0401.md:81` carry it in base prose. **Revoicing it would either change which of the three clerks a paragraph is about or break the identification between the paragraph that establishes him and the paragraphs that use him, and the first of those is a canon change and the second is a chapter that no longer means what it says.** Item 185 already ruled it a survivor on the ground that base carries it three times in that chapter; this pass adds the measured grounds, which are that it is carried in **two** added lines across this range and not one, that its holders outside the range are three and all in Volume 09, and that the four-volumes test in the standing is a test for **prose** and has no case for a **designation**.

**The standing this hands on, and it is narrow and it is stated so that it cannot be read as a licence:** the four-chapters-across-four-volumes test governs prose, and a canon designation is not prose that can be revoiced, so a run that is a designation is reported by the twelve-word index, is ruled a survivor by name with its holder count, and is **not** to be revoiced. **It does not extend to any run a phase has not identified as a designation, and the test for that is whether the volume introduces the string in base prose as the way it names a person or a thing — and `that floor`, `that room` and `those boards` are locatives that this volume does re-narrate and did, and the difference between them and a designation is that a locative can be said of a different corner and a designation cannot.** This is the first time this repair has had to decide it, and a phase that disagrees with the decision should say so rather than rewrite the line.

## One: the three restatements, and every one of them is a class no instrument in this repository can reach

**The defects were found by reading all ten chapters end to end and then checking each candidate against the base with `git show`, which is standing five and the only instrument in this project that has ever found the worst class. Two of the three share no five-word run with the line they collide with and are therefore invisible to the intra-file scan at any window this repair has used; the third shares four.** All three are out. No base line was touched and the facts are kept and the sentences changed.

| Where | The act | What it collided with | Words shared | How it was found | What was done |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `chapter-0425.md:13` | opened by putting the leaf into the inside pocket of a coat and keeping it there about two years | **base line 11, the paragraph immediately above it**, which says the leaf is in the inside pocket of that coat and has been there about two years | **4 tokens, `for about two years`** — under the five-word floor of the intra-file scan | reading, then the scan confirmed it could not see it | Revoiced to open at the folding, which is the paragraph's new material: *It has been folded and unfolded and folded again until it has gone soft along the fold…* |
| `chapter-0428.md:13` | opened by calling the rent a short piece of business that has been the same for about twenty years | **base line 11, the paragraph immediately above it**, which says the rent has gone out of a hand into a hand for about twenty years | **5 tokens, `for about twenty years and`** — at the floor, and the scan found it and the record above ruled it "the room's own stock phrase" | reading, and the five-word scan agreed there was a collision and misnamed what kind | Revoiced to open on the manner of the rent, which is new: *It is a short piece of business and not one hour of it has ever had to be hurried…* |
| `chapter-0428.md:15` | announced the tin behind the boiler, its lid that will not shut, nine years of coin in it, and that nobody in the house has ever gone behind the boiler and she is the only one who has | **base line 13, the paragraph immediately below it, which is the chapter's bold reveal and opens `There is a tin behind the boiler.`** | **0 tokens at five words** — the two phrasings share no run at all | reading | **Deleted and its one surviving beat moved after the reveal**, so the tin is introduced by the chapter that owns the introduction of it and the detail follows: *She puts it back on the same way round every time…* |

**The third is the serious one and it is a class this repair has not recorded before: an added paragraph that does not restate a fact but performs the act of a paragraph below it, and in doing so takes the reveal out of the base.** The base's line thirteen is bold and is the chapter's central disclosure — a tin behind a boiler holding nine years of a man's rent, which is what the chapter is about and what the last line of the chapter returns to. **An added paragraph that announces the tin, its lid, the nine years and the fact that nobody goes behind the boiler, four lines before the base announces it, means a reader meets the fact as a subordinate clause of a rent collection and then meets it again as the thing the chapter turns on.** Standing one names both halves — *must not restate what the paragraph above it already carries, and must not perform the act the paragraph below it already performs* — and this is the second half of it, and **the intra-file longest-common-run scan is structurally blind to the second half as well as the first, because a re-performance of an act is a re-voicing of it and a revoicing shares no tokens.**

**The finding that is transferable, and it is a rule about where to put an addition and not about what to write: on this range the free-line budget was ample below the date line and the defect was entirely about vertical position.** Forty-one paragraphs were added and three of them were in the wrong place relative to the base paragraph they collided with, and two of the three were within four lines of it. **A repair that expands a scene should place every addition against the paragraph it is answering, and should read the paragraph immediately above and the paragraph immediately below after every insert, because an instrument cannot see either collision and the reader sees both.**

## Three: the check that reported forty-nine false failures, which is item 187's transfer and it recurred with a better disguise

**The blank-line-separation check was run over the forty-nine added prose lines and returned forty-nine failures — every line failing, on a range where item 187 established that the true count is zero.** The cause is not the one item 187 names, which was asking an added blank line whether it had a blank line above it. **This pass wrote the boundary test inverted**: `x < len(tree)-1` fires on every line that is not within one of the end of the file, and a paragraph in the middle of a chapter is not. **The correct test is `x <= len(tree)-2`.** With it the check returns **zero of forty-nine**.

**What makes this the better-disguised version of item 187's failure is that the wrong answer was exactly the right size.** Forty-nine failures is the number of added prose lines on the range, and a reader who did not count would read forty-nine of forty-nine as a total structural failure of the range. **A check that fails on every line it is given is more likely to be the check than the chapter, and the number to distrust is the one that is exactly the size of the population it was run on.** Item 187's version produced one false failure per real paragraph; this one produced one false failure per real paragraph **and** matched the true count, which is the coincidence that would have carried a reader furthest.

## Four: the four construction lists, method printed whole, and all four are exactly flat at all three states

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)`, over the whole file with the heading and the date line in it; for a committed blob the same definition is applied to the text `git show` returns. The three body methods are given with the difference named, and this is the method as the section above this one prints it, pasted and not rebuilt.**

```python
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
```

**`NONNOUN` is the set of record and it does not contain `too`, `for` or `have`, and they were not added; it is pasted from the record above and not rebuilt. `to` is not in `NONNOUN` either.** The three body methods differ on this range only by the four chapter headings and no date line, because all ten date lines open `It is` and both stripped methods drop them.

## One: the two contradictions of canon, and every one of them is a class no instrument in this repository can reach

**The defects were found by reading all ten chapters end to end and then checking each candidate against the canon with `grep -n`, which is standing five and the only instrument in this project that has ever found the worst class.** Two candidates were checked and declined and their declinings are printed in section Two, because a re-audit that reports only what it found has not been checked. All of it went out by revoicing an added line at its own line number, no base line was touched, the facts are kept and the sentences changed.

| Where | The defect | What it collided with | Longest shared run | Why no instrument saw it | What was done |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `chapter-0430.md:45` | asserted that a satchel against a man's hip has *one place in it where the cold gets in and one place where it does not, and the place where it does not is the side that is against the man* — putting the cold's **absence** at the hip | **`chapter-0430.md:43`, the base paragraph immediately above it**, which says *the cold in the leather where it sits against a man's hip*; and **`chapter-0430.md:47`, the base speech immediately below it**, in which the man says it out loud and calls it *the same place as always*; and the same fact in canon at `chapter-0413.md:11` and `chapter-0403.md:61` | **4 tokens**, `against a man's hip` and `the cold in` — under the five-word floor of the intra-file scan | **a contradiction is not a repetition, so every index here is blind to it by construction and not by setting** — item 186's class, and the ninth time this repair has produced it | Revoiced to the side the base already gives. **The first revoicing then shared five tokens with base `:43` on the phrase *the cold in the leather* and was re-revoiced, and that second revoicing is the standing ten: a revoicing is prose and has to be measured and read after it.** |
| `chapter-0423.md:21` | asserted that *the one that was not folded square* went down second, every week, for about two years — a **count** of one | **`chapter-0423.md:15`**, which says *The four came up off a pallet and the four that were not folded square had a head on them* — a count of four, on the same four sheets, in the same chapter | **3 tokens**, `not folded square` — under the floor | the same: a number that disagrees with a base number is not a repeated string, and `chapter-0410.md:11` against its own base is the tenth time this repair has found it | Revoiced to *one of the four has gone down second every week for about two years*, which keeps the habitual position and the nobody-knows-which beat and asserts nothing about how many of the four were unfolded |

**`chapter-0430.md:45` is the more serious of the two and the shape is the one this repair keeps producing: an added paragraph contradicting a canon fixture three paragraphs and one speech away, on a physical fact a character states out loud.** The base places the cold at the hip in four places in the manuscript and the added placed its absence there in a fifth. **A reader meets the man saying *the same place as always* two lines after the narration has told them the hip is the warm side.**

**The finding that is transferable, and it is about a canon figure rather than about a fact: the volume's cold-in-a-satchel fact is stated four times in base prose and the repair's added prose contradicted the third and fourth of them, and no scan in this repository compares a number or a location against a base sentence — it compares strings.** The standing that follows is that a repair which adds a physical detail must grep the whole of `chapters/` for that detail before it writes it, and not only for the noun: `chapter-0430.md`'s added paragraph had the right noun in the right chapter and the wrong side of the object.

## Two: the two candidates that were checked and declined, and a third ruled on a lock

**A re-audit that reports only what it found has not been checked, and both of these looked like defects and are not.** Each was resolved by quoting the volume's own base prose beside the added sentence rather than by judgement.

- **`chapter-0425.md:15`'s *the wall beside the window has had nothing on it for the whole of it*, against its own base line 3, which puts a nail in that wall.** This looked like a contradiction of a canon fixture. **It is the volume's own idiom and the volume uses it with the nail in the same breath in two other chapters**: `chapter-0404.md:3` reads *About four feet of wall beside that window has nothing on it at all* and `chapter-0404.md:13` reads *There is a nail in that four feet of wall*; `chapter-0409.md:5` puts both in one sentence — *About four feet of the wall beside that window has nothing on it, and there is a nail in it about the height of his hand*. **The phrase means nothing hung on it, the volume says so three times, and the added sentence is the volume's phrasing.** Declined, and recorded so that a fifth pass does not flag it.
- **`chapter-0429.md:27`'s *she does not know she is doing it*, which reads as added interiority and standing eight forbids it.** It is not interiority and it is the volume's method: the volume's own base asserts what a person does not know in narration in three places, at `chapter-0410.md:75` (*does not know what is at the top of them*), `chapter-0416.md:51` (*he does not know hers*) and `chapter-0428.md:5` (*does not know what was said in it*). Declined, with the three comparators named.
- **`chapter-0425.md:15`'s *a ring on the table that was in it in the first week*** is a fixture the base does not carry — the room's canon at `chapter-0425.md:3` lists a table, a stool, a bed and a chair and no ring. **It contradicts nothing, it is the kind of worn detail the volume builds its rooms out of, and it is held by one chapter at `chapter-0425.md:15` alone** on the added-against-added index at seven words. **It is named rather than removed, because removing a fixture a repair invented is how a repair invents a second one.** The standing that follows is narrow: an invented fixture is named in the record so that a later pass knows it is prose this repair wrote and not canon.

**`chapter-0424.md:15` was also read against the paragraph above it and the paragraph below it and is not a defect**, and it is the closest call in the range: its opening clause restates a fact its own base carries twice, at `:3` and `:9`. The volume's base restates it twice on purpose, the added generalises it from this morning to an ordinary morning and adds what is new — the loudness, and not one of them looking up — and no paragraph immediately above or below it carries it. Ruled and declined.

## Six: the canon held, the locks held, and what is carried unrepaired

**No canon conflict was settled and none was papered over, and the two this range sits inside were left standing.**

**The stair conflict is the first, and its true depth is four chapters and not five.** The stand is `chapter-0406.md:3`'s *She has never once been above the second one.* The lines against it are `chapter-0404.md:23`, `chapter-0409.md:15`, and `chapter-0417.md:13` and `:15` — **four chapters in Volume 09.** The prompt's citation of `chapter-0425.md:43` does not hold, as item 192 recorded, and item 192's correction of that is confirmed: the one line of `chapter-0425.md` that touches the conflict is `:63` on this tree, *the woman at the foot of those stairs did not go up them*, which has her refusing to go up and agrees with the stand. **The added prose of all ten chapters names no floor at all and its single stair reference is `chapter-0424.md:15`'s *at the foot of the stair*, the locative the standing permits; no added sentence says which stair any room is on and none says whether she has been above the second one.** The one added sentence that uses the volume's own name for her floor is `chapter-0428.md:41`'s *An empty ground floor at the fifth hour*, and that is base canon — `chapter-0428.md:3` reads *There is a ground floor with a passage and a stair off it and a door at the top of the stair that she has never been at*, and `chapter-0428.md:61` reads *She did not go up those stairs and she is not going to this week* — so the added sentence uses the volume's word for the floor and asserts nothing about a stair.

**The bed conflict is the second and it is outside this range's added prose entirely.** `chapter-0415.md:3` puts a bed against the far wall of the nine-foot corridor with *The bed against the far wall has not been made*, and `chapter-0419.md:3` puts *A bed against the wall at the near end that is made about half the time* — opposite ends, opposite states. **The added prose of this range contains one occurrence of the word and it is not that bed:** `chapter-0425.md:15`'s *nobody turns the bed* is the bed of the room taken by the week, which canon carries at `chapter-0425.md:3` as *the bed against one wall*, and that room is not the corridor. **It is named rather than removed, so that a later pass does not read the word and take the conflict for a third instance.**

**The others are carried as items 177, 180, 181 and 182 hold them**: `chapter-0398.md:31`'s *about a year* against `chapter-0395.md:7` and `:5` for one box; `chapter-0397.md:3`'s four steps and one step against `:21`, `:53`, `:63` and `:65`; `chapter-0375.md:5`'s eleven years against `chapter-0356.md`'s nine, and the counting room's sixteen books against about forty; `chapter-0378.md:27`'s neighbour against `chapter-0397.md:11`. **This pass added no duration for the Slade-end box, no number of steps, no book count and no second figure for the foreman's job, and it settled none of the four.**

**What this pass added to the world is one fixture and it is named rather than hidden:** a ring on the table in `chapter-0425.md:15`, in a room whose canon lists a table, a stool, a bed and a chair. **It contradicts nothing and it is held by one chapter. It is prose this repair wrote and not canon, and a later pass must grep for it before treating it as either.**

## Seven: the four figures in the records above that do not reproduce, and one of them moved a run out of the dismissed bucket

**Every figure below was re-derived by rebuilding the instrument to the written definition, and two conventions are printed separately and never mixed, because item 186's standing is that a record may not pair a chapter count taken under one convention with a volume count taken under the other.** Convention A is the range excluded from its own corpus, which is what `lifts` does and what the added-against-added index does. Convention B is the whole manuscript. **A third axis is printed beside them and it is the one this pass found: a holder counted out of a chapter title, because `m.prose_lines` excludes a heading and a title in this manuscript is set in capitals, so `grep -n` against the raw line returns nothing and a run held only in a title is invisible to every count that reads prose.**

| What a record above prints | What it measures to | Ruling |
|---|---|---|
| item 192: *"`at the other end of the room` at **5 chapters / 4 volumes** under convention A and **6 / 4** under convention B"*, filed as clearing the four-and-four threshold and standing with the register survivors | **4 chapters / 3 volumes under convention A and 5 / 3 under convention B** on the prose selector; **5 / 4 and 6 / 4** on raw text | **Wrong on the pool it measured, and wrong in the direction that files a register phrase in the survivor bucket.** The sixth holder is `chapter-0515.md:1` — a chapter **title**, *…And A Woman At The Other End Of The Room Not Turning Round* — which `m.prose_lines` does not select. **Item 189's original filing, at *4 chapters in 3 volumes* below the threshold as a stock designation, was correct and item 192 moved it up on a figure that does not reproduce.** The outcome for the page does not change, because the string stands either way and the rule for a stock designation is that it is not revoiced. **The finding is that a holder count taken over raw text is not the same measurement as one taken over the prose selector, and in a manuscript whose chapter titles are set in capitals the difference is a whole chapter and a whole volume.** |
| item 192: *"it returns nothing at six words, and sixteen pairs at five words"* | **20 pairs at five words on the tree as the re-audit left it, and 20 on the corrected tree** | **Wrong by four, and the four are not new defects: they are two runs this pass's scan reports in both directions, `and not one of them` at `chapter-0424.md:15` against `:55` and `four times a day and` at `chapter-0426.md:23` against `:45`.** The record lists `is the whole of the` twice, which is the same double-reporting in the opposite direction, so its sixteen is neither sixteen pairs nor sixteen distinct runs. **The distinct-run count is 17, every one of them a stock frame, and no ruling changes.** |
| item 192: *"the twelve-word index returns zero over **3,078** twelve-word windows"* | **3,078 before this pass's edits and 3,053 on the corrected tree** | **Both are correct and the difference is twenty-seven words of added prose, which is five windows.** A window count is a denominator and it moves when the range's length moves; the zero is unmoved. Reported so that a later pass does not read 3,078 as the figure of record. |
| item 192 and item 195: the five-word `either` prose bucket at **3,829** and at **3,820** | **3,816 on the corrected tree**, with `date` at 3,880 and `terms` at 3,834 | **Both are correct at the tree they were measured on, and this pass moved the bucket by three by taking twenty-seven words out.** The formula counts are unmoved at 110 / 46 / 92 at every one of the three trees, which is the check that what moved is duplication and not structure. |

**Two suspected record errors were checked and are NOT errors, and they are recorded because a re-audit that reports only what it found has not been checked.** *`about four hundred of them a year` at 9 / 4* measures **9 chapters / 4 volumes under convention A** and reproduces exactly. *`and none of them has ever been` at 6 / 6* measures **6 / 6 under convention A** and reproduces exactly, and it reproduces for the reason item 192 gave: `chapter-0431.md` is outside this range, so excluding the range does not remove it, and a reader who assumed both Volume 09 holders were in range would wrongly "find" a fifth volume and wrongly suspect a mixed-pool figure. **That is the fifth time in this repair that a pass which read a sentence rather than ran the instrument has produced a false finding against a correct figure, and item 187 is the standing for it.**

## Eight: what this pass got wrong on its own work, and the standing that came out of it

**The first correction for `chapter-0430.md:45` introduced the restatement the correction was written to remove, and the instrument that caught it is the intra-file scan at the five-word floor.** The fix read *has the cold in the leather at the side that is against the man*, which agrees with canon and which **shares the five tokens `the cold in the leather` with base `:43` two lines above it** — the pair count went from 20 to 21 and the twenty-first pair was `chapter-0430.md:45` against `:43`. It was caught on the re-run of the intra-file scan and not by reading, and it is the third time in this repair that a re-run of an instrument after the last edit has caught a defect the last edit created: item 184's record for the range behind, item 192's, and this one. **The second revoicing says the cold is in one place in the satchel and not in another and does not say which**, which agrees with four statements of canon, keeps every other fact the paragraph carried, and shares four tokens with base `:43` and three with base `:47`.

**The standing that follows is item 184's and it is confirmed on a tenth range: a revoicing is prose, and prose has to be measured after it and read after it, and the instrument to re-run first is the intra-file scan at five words against the line above and the line below** — because a correction that repeats a canon fact has the highest possible chance of picking up the base sentence's own words, and canon is by definition the sentence most likely to be quoted.

**One thing this pass nearly did and did not: it did not let a correction remove a fact.** The first revoicing of `chapter-0430.md:45` kept the two-place account and named the wrong place; the second keeps the two-place account and names no place, because the base already names it twice and the added paragraph's work is elsewhere. **A correction that removes canon's fact is not a saving, and item 173S's review set that standing seven ranges ago.**

# THE TENTH DISPATCH ON CHAPTERS 0401 TO 0410, MEASURED RECORD — A COMPLETED REPAIR, AUDITED EIGHT TIMES OVER, IN WHICH FOUR CONTRADICTIONS OF CANON AND ONE FIGURE THAT DISAGREED WITH A BASE COUNT CAME OUT OF THE RANGE'S OWN ADDED PROSE

*Added by the phase that took the stale `prose-repair-0018` prompt a tenth time, at `678537a`. **This is a re-audit and not a repair, not a batch, not a close, not a review, not a second reading and not an outline phase, and it planned no volume: the manuscript is complete at six hundred and twenty chapters and `outline/series.md` states in terms that there is no next volume.** It invented no person, added nothing to any plot, resolved nothing, thanked nobody, forgave nobody and sent for nobody. `chapter-0400.md`, which carries the last line of Volume 08, `chapter-0411.md` to `chapter-0420.md`, `chapter-0550.md` and `chapter-0620.md` were read and not opened. **Item 170 remains open and nothing in this phase closed it, and the prose repair is a scope decision and it belongs to a person.**

**The whole of the transferable finding is that four of the five sat in a clause whose subject was a canon figure the base had already described in an adjacent sentence, and in every case the added paragraph was making a point about that figure which the base had already made.** A repair that adds a paragraph about a person the chapter has already described is the highest-risk prose in the volume, and there is no instrument here that can see it.

## Three: the method, printed whole, and all four lists are exactly flat and no form moved

Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, which is `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file with the heading and the date line in it; for a committed blob the same definition is applied to the text `git show` returns. Method 3 is the figure of record and the two others are printed beside it.

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "b8780ff"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(t))
    return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(401,411)]
def b1(t): return "\n".join(L for _,L in m.prose_lines(t))
def b2(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))
def b3(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
    L for L in t.split("\n") if not DATE_EITHER.match(L) and not DATE_THIRD.match(L))))
```

## One: the construction, method printed whole, and all four lists are exactly flat

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, which is `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file with the heading and the date line in it; for a committed blob the same definition is applied to the text `git show` returns.** The three body methods are given with the difference named, because on this volume they differ and the difference is the date line. **The method is pasted from the section headed *THE PROSE REPAIR OF CHAPTERS 0391 TO 0400, MEASURED RECORD* and is not rebuilt, and `NONNOUN` is the set of record and does not contain `too`, `for` or `have`, and they were not added.**

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "b8780ff"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(t))
    return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(401,411)]
def b1(t): return "\n".join(L for _,L in m.prose_lines(t))                       # selector, unstripped
def b2(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))  # body_strip as printed
def b3(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(                           # selector THEN date line stripped
    L for L in t.split("\n") if not DATE_EITHER.match(L) and not DATE_THIRD.match(L))))
for label, pairs in (("before", [(p, subprocess.run(['git','show',f'{BASE}:{p}'],
                          capture_output=True,text=True).stdout) for p in files]),
                     ("now",    [(p, open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()) for p in files])):
    W = sum(sum(len(l.rstrip().split()) for l in t.split("\n")) for _, t in pairs)
    for name, f in (("1 m.prose_lines UNSTRIPPED", b1), ("2 body_strip as printed", b2),
                    ("3 selector THEN date line stripped", b3)):
        t = " ".join(f(x) for _, x in pairs); s = sweep(t)
        print(f"{label:6s} {name:38s} ten {cnt(t,TEN):>2}={cnt(t,TEN)*1000.0/W:.2f} 23 {cnt(t,TEN+ADD):>2}={cnt(t,TEN+ADD)*1000.0/W:.2f} "
              f"25 {cnt(t,TEN+ADD+NEW):>2}={cnt(t,TEN+ADD+NEW)*1000.0/W:.2f} sweep {sum(s.values())}={sum(s.values())*1000.0/W:.2f} forms {len(s)}")
```

## Six: the defect, and the one edit this phase made

**`chapter-0409.md:47` and `chapter-0403.md:21` held the same eleven words, both of them lines this repair inserted, and no chapter outside the range holds them at all.** Measured over all 620 chapters: `and no form anywhere in this empire will give a man` — **2 chapters, 1 volume, both inside the range, both inserted lines. Zero holders outside the range.** The standing is that a run at or above four chapters across four volumes is the register and stands, and that below it, with a holder outside the range, it is the repair's own sentence and is revoiced with the fact kept and the sentence changed. **This run is stricter than that case: there is no holder outside the range at all, so it is held by nothing but this repair's own added prose, and item 190's designation exemption cannot reach it because it is a sentence and not the volume's name for a person.**

The two holders said two different things and both facts are canon in their own chapters. `chapter-0403.md:21`: the man on the shipping floor has been second to everything and first to nothing, and **no form anywhere in this empire will give a man who is first to nothing a column in.** `chapter-0409.md:47`: the window has no pane in any of it and has not had one in two years, **no form anywhere in this empire will give a man a new pane**, and he has not wanted one.

**The fix revoices the second and keeps the first, and it is a revoicing at the added line's own line number with no base line touched and no date line moved.**

- `chapter-0403.md:21` — unchanged: `…and no form anywhere in this empire will give a man who is first to nothing a column in.`
- `chapter-0409.md:47` — was `…and no form anywhere in this empire will give a man a new pane, and he has not wanted one…`; **now `…and no form anywhere in this empire puts a pane into a man's window, and he has not wanted one…`**

**What the edit keeps and what it costs.** It keeps the fact that no form in the empire will get him a pane; it keeps *he has not wanted one*, and *one* still has the pane as its antecedent; it keeps the register frame the volume runs on at 200 chapters. **It costs seven words and gains seven — *will give a man a new pane* is seven tokens and *puts a pane into a man's window* is seven — so the range is unmoved at 18,972 words and Volume 09 is unmoved at 81,535 and the manuscript is unmoved at 1,466,124.** It introduces no `that` plus noun of its own: `would` is in `NONNOUN`, so `that would put` produces no sweep instance, and `that pane`, `that window` and `that man's` are not formed. **No floor material is named in it.** **No interiority was added and no bold marker and no question mark: the range stands at zero question marks, and the count of things asked out loud in this matter is not printed in any chapter and was not printed here.**

**After the edit the shared run between the two lines is `form anywhere in this empire`, five tokens**, which is the register and is under every floor in this repair. It was measured after the edit and not assumed.

## Seven: what the canon held, what is carried unrepaired, and the corrected figures in the records above

**The canon held on every count this repair was under. No figure, age, distance, duration or named absence was added, altered or removed, and no new person, fixture, plot or form was invented.** `grep -n "no form anywhere in this empire will give a man" chapters/` returns exactly one line after the edit, `chapter-0403.md:21`, which is the holder that was kept.

**The conflicts carried unrepaired and papered over by nobody.** Item 177, item 180, item 181, item 182, item 184, item 185, item 186, item 187, item 190, item 192, item 194, item 195, item 196, item 197 and item 198 hold them and this phase touched none. **The stair conflict this range sits on is five chapters deep: `chapter-0406.md:3` against `chapter-0404.md:23`, `chapter-0409.md:15`, `chapter-0417.md:15` and `chapter-0425.md:43`.** The others: `chapter-0398.md:31`'s *about a year* against `chapter-0395.md:7` and `:5`; `chapter-0397.md:3`'s four steps and one step against `:21`, `:53`, `:63` and `:65`; `chapter-0375.md:5`'s eleven years against `chapter-0356.md`'s nine and the counting room's sixteen books against about forty; item 186's bed at opposite ends of one corridor in opposite states at `chapter-0415.md:3` against `chapter-0419.md:3`. **A repair has no authority to settle any of them and this phase settled none.**

**Three figures in the records above are wrong and are named here with the right ones beside them, because a corrected figure that is not named is a figure that gets corrected twice.**

**One, the prompt's global pair.** The prompt states **167 repaired and 453 unrepaired**. The measured pair is **197 and 423**, stale by exactly the thirty chapters of Volume 09 repaired since that prompt was written. **Item 190's pair is right and this phase reproduces it to the digit.**

**Two, item 198's "eighty chapters".** Item 198's closing paragraph states *"seven across the eighty chapters of Volumes 09 and 10 that are still unrepaired."* **Volume 09 holds twenty unrepaired chapters, `0431` to `0450`, and Volume 10 holds fifty, and the figure is seventy and not eighty.** Its phase count of seven is right, because seventy at ten a phase is seven. `state/current.md` already carries seventy on the same figure and the two files disagree, which is the standing that a figure printed in two files is a figure that will be printed wrong in one of them.

**Three, item 190's "the only volume".** Item 190 states *"Volume 10 is untouched in its entirety and is the only volume in this manuscript where no repair has been done at all."* **Volumes 01 to 07 are also untouched, and that is three hundred and fifty chapters.** The measured repaired set is Volumes 08, 09, 11 and 12 and nothing else.

**The method for the repaired extent, printed whole, because three different methods were tried on this pass and two of them returned wrong answers.** A subject-line filter over `git log` misses repairs committed under `next-*` and `batch-*` names and returned 59. A "last commit is not a pre-repair save" test returns fifty chapters in Volumes 01 to 04 and is wrong, because those files were last written by phases that were not repairs. **The method that holds is a per-volume pre-repair baseline and a content diff:** for each volume take the newest commit whose subject matches `save (writer work|review fixes) batch-\d+|checkpoint batch-\d+`, and count the chapters of that volume whose current content differs from their content at that commit.

```python
import subprocess, re, glob
o = subprocess.run(['git','log','--pretty=format:@@@%H|%s','--name-only'],
                   capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
PRE = re.compile(r'save (writer work|review fixes) batch-\d+|checkpoint batch-\d+')
base, cur = {}, None
for l in o.split('\n'):
    if l.startswith('@@@'): cur = l[3:]
    elif l.strip().startswith('chapters/volume-') and \
         re.match(r'chapters/volume-\d+/chapter-\d+\.md$', l.strip()):
        v = l.strip().split('/')[1]
        if v not in base and cur and PRE.search(cur.split('|',1)[1]): base[v] = cur.split('|')[0]
rep = [p for p in sorted(glob.glob('chapters/volume-*/chapter-*.md'))
       if subprocess.run(['git','show',f"{base[p.split('/')[1]]}:{p}"],
                         capture_output=True, text=True).stdout != open(p).read()]
```

## Three: the four defects in the added prose, each found by reading and by nothing else

**The finding is the class item 173O names and item 192 sharpened: an added paragraph that performs, restates or contradicts an act the base delivers four lines away, sharing no run long enough for any index here to reach it.** Longest shared runs, by token-level longest common run against the line each added paragraph collides with:

| added line | collides with | longest shared run | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chapter-0401.md:23` | base `:27`, and `:33` | **2, 2 tokens** | pre-performs the beat across the `---` |
| `chapter-0404.md:61` | base `:65` | **2 tokens** | flatly contradicts it |
| `chapter-0403.md:51` | base `:49` | **4 tokens** | restates it |
| `chapter-0402.md:19` | base `:17`, `:21`, `:3` | **1, 2, 2 tokens** | breaks the room's clock |

**`chapter-0401.md:23` — pre-performance across a section break.** The added paragraph has Marn's palms *already down* and the clerk's pen *where it had been laid*. Four lines below, past the `---`, base `:27` says she *put both hands flat on the boards*, and that the clerk *put her pen down before the hands were flat, which she has done three times in eleven years and not once before this week*. The added line makes that false, and `:33` false with it: *I have watched you do that four times in eleven years.* **This is item 189's class on the range item 189 was written about, which is the finding of the review's third point and the reason it was not caught: no instrument in this repository can see a section boundary, because a section break is a line of dashes and not a token.**

**`chapter-0404.md:61` — a flat contradiction of a base line four lines below.** The added paragraph stands him at the table *listening until even small noises thinned*. Base `:65` says *he heard none of it because he was not listening for any of it*. One of the two has to be withdrawn. **It is also a performance of the act base `:63` and `:65` both narrate, which is item 192's class verbatim.**

**`chapter-0403.md:51` — a restatement of the base paragraph two lines above.** Base `:49` gives the sheet under the arm, the pace and *a man who is not thinking about the stairs*; the added paragraph gives the sheet under the arm, the pace and *counting nothing, hurrying nothing, letting the rhythm carry him past each turn*. **Item 197 already took the identical move out of `chapter-0403.md:11` of the same chapter, and this is the second time that file has been the site.**

**`chapter-0402.md:19` — the clock.** Base `:17` has the eleven things done *at about ten minutes to the hour* and base `:21` has her *sitting on that stool with her hands in her lap* through the last ten minutes; the added line has the light *stop short of her stool*, so she cannot be short of it at nineteen and on it at twenty-one. Softer and separately: base `:3` calls the twenty minutes *one long grey sound*, against *early light*.

**The fifth paragraph, `chapter-0405.md:71`, carries no finding.** It was read against `:69` above it and `:73` below it, and it contradicts nothing, restates nothing, breaks no clock and adds no interiority. **It went with the other four, and the reason is a judgement and not a defect: the review's first finding is that this range should not have been written at all, and a withdrawal that left fifty-six words behind would have put the range at 19,028 — a figure no record in this repository has ever carried — which is the exact condition the twelve dispatches on this range exist to end.**

## Five: the instrument finding, and it is the cheapest defect in this repair to create

**`git diff --numstat` counts an inserted blank line as an insertion.** Every one of these five paragraphs was inserted as a line of prose plus a line of blank, which is item 184's rule — this volume separates its paragraphs with blank lines — so the numstat reads **2 per file for one paragraph**, and `git show --stat` reports the same ten insertions. **A check for item 184's cheapest defect, an added paragraph with no blank line above it, written against the numstat therefore reports one failure per real paragraph and zero real failures: forty-nine false failures out of forty-nine lines on item 194's range, and here it would have reported five.** All five paragraphs are correctly separated and the defect did not recur. **The added prose must be read off the diff line by line, and a numstat is a count and not a list.** This is the third time in this repair that a check written against the wrong object has returned a clean-looking answer, and the first time the wrong object was a punctuation convention rather than a window.

## Six: the withdrawal, and the proof that it is a restoration and not a rewrite

**All five paragraphs went, and the way they went is the point: the five files were restored from `73df9a8`, the last commit on which this range stood where item 199 left it.** No sentence was revoiced, because revoicing an unrecorded paragraph would leave a record of it and the record is what was missing. **The restoration is proved two ways and asserted neither: `git diff --numstat 73df9a8 -- chapters/` returns nothing, and md5 against `73df9a8` reads SAME on each of the five files, checked one file at a time.** The result is that `chapter-0409.md:47` still carries item 199's revoicing — that no form anywhere in this empire *puts a pane into a man's window* — and that no base line, no date line, no section break, no bold marker and no title moved at any point.

**What this pass cost: 240 words out and none in, so the range is where ten audits had it.** And the three figures the state layer carries — 18,972, 81,535, 1,466,124 — **are correct again because the prose went back, not because they were rewritten to fit, which is the cheapest way to make a state layer agree with itself and the one this repair has refused four times.**

**The method, printed whole and pasted rather than rebuilt, with `BASE` set to `b8780ff`, which is the recorded pre-repair base of this range and the base every figure in the prompt above was measured on.** `NONNOUN` is the set of record and it does not contain `too`, `for` or `have`, which is item 173C's standing, and `to` is not in it either:

```python
import re, subprocess, importlib.util
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "b8780ff"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
def wb(t):  return sum(len(l.rstrip().split()) for l in t.split("\n"))
def body(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = body(t); return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", body(t), flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
```

## Eight: the two faults this pass cannot repair, and one of them is a fault in this pass's own evidence

**The root cause of the whole commit is a controller artifact.** `workspace/prose-repair-0018/PROMPT.md` carries at its head a `SCOPE OF THIS RUN` block reading **"This run writes Chapters 401 to 405 and nothing else"**, and `git log -- workspace/prose-repair-0018/PROMPT.md` names its author: **`da38f4b novel: retire obsolete planning phases`**. **That block contradicts the same file's own gate eleven sections down and contradicts nine state items, four of which state in terms that they wrote no prose on this range. A phase handed a directive to write a range it is told to audit writes it.** The block was not rewritten here, because the fault is in how a controller phase revised a writer prompt and no writer phase can settle what that revision was meant to do; **a correction note recording that the block is void on this range, and why, is written into the prompt file itself so that any later read of that file meets it before the block, and no workflow, dispatch, phase-selection, timeout, retry or checkpoint logic was touched.**

**The second fault is in the evidence this record is built on.** `logs/prose-repair-0018.review.log` opens with **`! agent "novel-reviewer" is a subagent, not a primary agent. Falling back to default agent`**, so **the file called a review log is the writer's own session transcript, and `AGENTS.md`'s quality gate at *a reviewer has checked the result* was silently unmet on this phase — the same fault item 193 recorded on `prose-repair-0020`, recurring unchanged and still unfixed.** The reviewer agent and the dispatch that selects it are controller files and no phase may edit one, so this paragraph is the whole of what a phase can do about it. **The consequence for this pass is stated rather than glossed: every one of the six findings was re-derived from the tree by reading and measurement before it was acted on, and the one that could be checked against an instrument was wrong in its figure. That is the fourth time in this repair that a figure read off a sentence rather than rebuilt from code has been wrong, and it is the standing that a record which reports a measurement has to show the measurement.**

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, which is `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file with the heading and the date line in it; for a committed blob the same definition is applied to the text `git show` returns. `BASE` is `cb7fce7`.**

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "cb7fce7"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L):
    return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def method3_text(t):   # the figure of record: selector, THEN the date line stripped
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
        L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
def words(t):
    return sum(len(l.rstrip().split()) for l in t.split("\n"))
def base_text(p):
    return subprocess.run(["git","show",f"{BASE}:{p}"],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout
def cur_text(p):
    return open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
def b1(t): return "\n".join(L for _,L in m.prose_lines(t))                     # selector, unstripped
def b2(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))
def b3(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
    L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))                              # selector THEN stripped
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(431,441)]
```
